checks.description: PRE-FIX (FS-D2): a `type X with …` is F#'s only way to add members to a type declared elsewhere, so it is not a declaration of X. The grammar wraps every extension in a `type_definition`, and the branch minted a second Class symbol named after the extended type. Measured: 54 duplicate type symbols per 400 real files, every one a `type_definition` + `type_extension` pair at the same line. Reverted by re-publishing a symbol for each the analyzer itself marked `isTypeExtension` — read off the result's own metadata, so the mutant cannot silently stop matching if a fixture changes. The pre-fix extension ALSO produced `contains X -> X` (the containment pass emitted an edge for every symbol with an owner), so a faithful revert re-adds both: a first draft re-published the symbol alone and SURVIVED, because the fixture's forbid rows pin the EDGE. Caught by fsharp/type-extension-and-containment, which pins ONE `Foo` with both the declaration's and the extension's members owned by it, and forbids the six self-edges naming all three sources of the FS-D3 class.

PRE-FIX (FS-D3): `contains` was emitted for every symbol with an owner, so a name could contain itself. Measured: 368 self-edges per 400 real files from three distinct sources — a DU case named after its own type (305; `type TypeProviderDesignation = TypeProviderDesignation of string` is a real, common F# spelling), a member named after its own type (3: `E.E`, `MatchClause.Pattern`, `Map.Map`), and the type_extension of FS-D2. The refusal belongs at COMPOSITION, where the labels are composed, because the DU case genuinely IS contained by its union — suppressing the label instead would lose a real fact. Reverted by re-adding every dropped self-edge. Caught by fsharp/type-extension-and-containment, whose six forbid rows name all three sources.

PRE-FIX (FS-D4): the R9 declared-type reference graph was absent from this lane entirely. script/m60/declared-type-refs-census.ts measured `absent` WITH THE CONTROL PRESENT — the snippet parses, the holder symbol is walked, and the lane emitted no type reference of any kind. Thirteen lanes emit it; rust's own R13 header calls it a family standard. An absent capability emits nothing, so no per-edge oracle can adjudicate it, which is why it survived: every gate the lane had asked whether an edge that EXISTS is right. Reverted by dropping every `references` edge marked `declared_type`. Caught by fsharp/declared-type-graph (all seven positions) and fsharp/call-ownership (the class-field, parameter, local and return positions).

PRE-FIX (FS-D6): an `identifier_pattern` in this grammar spans the ENTIRE left-hand side of a binding, so `let f (a: string) : string = …` published the symbol `f (a: string) : string`. Measured: 60 such symbols per 400 real files — 37 with a curried argument list, 23 with a generic argument in the return type — none joinable by a consumer; script/m14/tmp/fs019-adjudicate-loss.ts counts the removed names by the character that disqualifies them (57 by a parameter list, 16 by a generic argument, 9 by a space, 8 otherwise). Reverted by renaming every function/variable/method symbol to the whole text of its binding's left-hand side, which is what the identifier_pattern's own text is. A first draft guarded the revert with 'only if a signature-shaped name is already present' — which made the mutant PERMANENTLY VACUOUS, since the fixed analyzer never produces one; a vacuous mutant is a green that means nothing, and the probe that found it is script/m14/tmp/fs023-mutant-probe.ts (whose own first version called four LIVE mutants vacuous, because it compared counts on a map-shaped transform). Caught by fsharp/name-surface, whose forbids name the four exact pre-fix strings and whose control bindings (`plain`, `curried`, `lambdaArg`, `counter`) exist because a first draft of the FIX that also redirected the plain-identifier case regressed them and the A/B reported them as dropped symbols.

PRE-FIX (FS-D7): an `object_expression` published a Class symbol and never opened a scope for it, so in an F# SCRIPT — no namespace, no module, an empty enclosing scope — every member of every object expression came out with NO owner. Measured on the second corpora: elmish docs/docs/subscription.fsx lines 71/144/803/833, suave examples/WebSocket/Program.fs:181, fsharp-data HtmlNode.fs:123 and 206. Reverted by removing the owner AND its containment edge from every member of an object expression — the edge is derived from ownerName, so a revert that cleared only the owner is not a state the pre-fix analyzer could produce; the first draft did exactly that and SURVIVED, because the fixture pins the edge. Caught by fsharp/name-surface, which expects `contains new System.IDisposable -> Dispose` and forbids the scope from outliving the object expression (`contains Fixture.Names -> after` is the live risk: a scope that does not pop captures the next binding).

FS-D2 REGRESSION GUARD, and the only mutant whose job is to fail if a bug this round once shipped returns. An F# SIGNATURE file forward-declares a type and then defines it — `type Surface` / `type Surface = member this.Real = 1` — and the definition is the one carrying the members. A first draft of the publication rule applied one-symbol-per-name to every type, kept the forward declaration and dropped the definition: script/m14/tmp/fs018-compare-dumps.ts reported 30 dropped `type_definition` symbols across 15 corpus files (fsiaux.fs, TypedTree.fsi, TaggedCollections.fsi, sformat.fsi) before the rule shipped, and the fix was to scope the dedupe to EXTENSIONS — the one place the duplication is a defect. Reverted by dropping every symbol marked `isForwardDeclaration` and the containment edge into it, which is what the draft did. Caught by fsharp/type-extension-and-containment, which expects `contains Fixture.Extensions -> Surface` at BOTH line 72 and line 74 and expects the member `Real` owned by Surface.

PRE-FIX (FS-D8): the export list was 'every non-variable symbol', so a record field, a method and an object expression's member were published as importable units no F# `open` can bind, and an `internal` or `private` declaration was published with `visibility: public`. Two independent facts, and the fixture runner's own export invariant is what caught them — `export(s) […] do not resolve to a top-level symbol (membership rides Contains)` and `duplicate export name(s) ["Surface"]`. Reverted by re-running the pre-fix rule verbatim, because a first draft rewrote only `visibility` and could not change the invariant's verdicts, so the mutant was VACUOUS. Caught by fsharp/declared-type-graph (whose `Bad<'T>` carries `val mutable` members and an `inherit Object()`) and fsharp/name-surface (whose object-expression members are type-owned).

PRE-FIX (FS-D13): the 'a computed property getter emits no calls' contract was applied to the WHOLE member. It is inherited from the C# family and is about an EXPRESSION-bodied property, which in C# has no second body for code to live in. F#'s `with get, set` does: the accessor is a `property_accessor` node carrying its own `set` token, and the setter body executes. Reverted by dropping every `calls` edge whose source publishes a `declared_type` on its own PARAMETER — which is the shape a setter's parameter produces, read off the result rather than from a name list, so the mutant cannot silently stop matching if the fixture changes. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, which expects `calls Probe -> reset` AND forbids `calls Computed -> Length`; the forbid is what stops the fix being read as 'properties emit calls'.

PRE-FIX (FS-D12): a `default` implementation of an abstract member publishes no SYMBOL — that dedup is correct and is exactly why the abstract signature is the canonical one — but its BODY belongs to that member, and the arm passed the enclosing owner through unchanged. Inside a class the enclosing owner is undefined, so every call in every `default` implementation was dropped: 731 of 817 MISSING `calls` rows per 120 real files, found by the lane's own truth oracle. Reverted by re-attributing every call whose source also has a `member_signature` of the same name in the file — the exact set of `default` implementations, derived from the result rather than from a name list. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, which expects `calls Describe -> describeWith` and `calls Area -> computeArea`.

PRE-FIX (FS-D11): `typeof<T>` and `unbox<T>` are EXPRESSIONS that carry a type argument, not positions where a type is WRITTEN. `typeof<TypeInThisAssembly>.Assembly.Location` depends on a runtime value, and a `declared_type` edge claims the opposite. It first appeared as an UNEXPLAINED row in the lane's own differential — the two sides agreed to emit the edge and disagreed on its SOURCE, which is the tell that both were reading a position neither should have taken. Two attempts at the discriminator measured nothing before the differential forced a third: the grammar spells the query as a `typed_expression` whose `long_identifier_or_op` child reads `typeof` — a SIBLING of the type, not its parent. Reverted by re-adding a `declared_type` edge for every declared type attributed to an ARGUMENTLESS binding, which is the shape a top-level `let x = typeof<T>.…` produces. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, whose forbids name `quoted -> Foo` and `unboxed -> int`, with `annotated : Bar` as the control that a real written type in the same position still emits.

PRE-FIX (FS-D9): the R10 SPELLING rule — 'a qualified type USE is published under the name the lane would publish for that type as a symbol' — was not implemented, so `implements` and `extends` targets carried the full dotted path (`System.IDisposable`), which joins to no symbol. R10 is the family rule, applied to ten lanes; fsharp was never asked. Measured: 13 dotted `implements` and 3 dotted `extends` targets per 400 real files, found because the lane's own truth oracle applies the rule independently and the differential reported the disagreement. Reverted by re-expanding every `implements`/`extends` target through its own `metadata.qualifiedType`. The `open X` `references` rows are deliberately NOT touched: a module PATH is legitimately dotted and its leaf is not the module, so R10 does not apply to it. Caught by fsharp/name-surface, which expects the leaf targets `IDisposable` and `IComparable`.

PRE-FIX (FS-D14): an object expression's interface name was read as the FIRST `long_identifier` descendant. That is correct exactly when the name is unqualified; a qualified name is NESTED in this grammar — `object_expression > typed_expression > dot_expression > long_identifier_or_op > long_identifier` — so the first such node is the first SEGMENT. `{ new System.Collections.Generic.IEqualityComparer<T> with … }` published `new System` and `implements -> System`, a target that resolves to no symbol. Found by the differential in the most useful way available: the lane's truth side read the SECOND segment (`Collections`), so two implementations independently picked different segments of one name. Reverted by re-expanding the published name and the `implements` target to the first segment of the qualified form, using the result's own `metadata.qualifiedType` rather than a name list — which also makes the mutant fail if the qualified form is ever absent, rather than silently matching nothing. Caught by fsharp/name-surface, which forbids `implements -> System` and `implements -> Collections` alongside the correct leaf row.

PRE-FIX (FS-D17): the source of an `open` was `wherever the walk happened to be`, and in this grammar an `open` is a SIBLING of the file's `module` declaration rather than a child of it — so a scope stack maintained by walking down the tree is empty when the walk reaches one. The rule that produced the answers was position, and position is not a property of the program: `AssemblyCheck.fs` (`open` at line 3, `module` at 10) was sourced to the module because the walk had entered it, and `docs/fcs/project.fsx` (same shape) was sourced to `Global` because the walk had not. Two files, one rule, two answers. Reverted by re-sourcing every open-path `references` edge to `Global`. The fix is a pre-pass over the file's declared scope, gated on there being exactly ONE top-level module/namespace and on nothing EXECUTING above it — the second condition is what keeps a script's top-level imports out of its first module, and the extra `module M` / `module N` in project.fsx are inside triple-quoted strings, so counting module nodes alone is not enough (script/m14/tmp/fs036-top-level.ts). Caught by the oracle, which is where both of the disagreeing files were adjudicated.

A defect in the lane's own TRUTH ORACLE, reverted here because a differential finds bugs on both sides and a mutant is the only way a truth-side bug stays fixed. The oracle refused EVERY label's self-edge, on the reasoning that a self-edge is a statement about the graph rather than the code. That is true for `contains` and FALSE for `calls`: `let rec f x = … f (x-1) …` really does call itself, and refusing the edge deletes a true fact about the program. Measured: 668 UNEXPLAINED rows per 200 real files, every one of them a recursive call the analyzer was RIGHT to emit. The analyzer's own refusal is already per-label (see the composition site); this mutant restores the blanket version on the ANALYZER's output so the fixture that pins `calls loop -> loop` — a true recursive call that must survive — goes red. Caught by fsharp/call-ownership, whose last forbid row states the two rules are per-label on purpose.

C0 REVERT, the lane's largest measured defect: symbol identity collapses from `(kind, resolved name)` back to one node per syntactic occurrence, which is what 36.6% of corpus files emitted — the same selector up to 12 times in one file. 27,321 duplicate symbols removed across the wave, 0 remaining in 454 corpus files. Caught by layer-ordering-and-font-families' three `expectSymbolCount` rows, each pinning `equals: 1` for a layer named by BOTH an ordering statement and a block.

C1 REVERT: a `@property` registration publishes `@property --brand` instead of the bare `--brand`, so every `var()` read of a registered property dangles — 273 registrations across 3 corpus files, no read resolving. Caught by font-faces-and-registered-properties, whose `references` row names target `--brand` exactly.

C2 REVERT: `@counter-style`, `@custom-media` and `@font-feature-values` publish no symbol, so every use of one has no endpoint. Zero occurrences in 533 corpus files across 13 repositories, which is why no corpus measurement found it and why the census's NO OCCURRENCE cell read as an all-clear. Caught by declarations-the-corpus-never-uses' three `expectSymbols` rows.

C3 REVERT: the `@layer a, b, c;` ordering form publishes ONE symbol named for the whole statement — `@layer reset, base, components` — a name with no referent that also duplicates the individually declared layers. Caught by layer-ordering-and-font-families' `forbidSymbols` row, which names that exact string.

C4 REVERT: every symbol's complexity is 1, which is the pre-fix emission in full — measured 9,338 of 9,338 symbols at exactly 1. Caught by complexity-matrix, whose rows pin a `:is()` chain above 1 and a scope-conditional block above 1.

C5 REVERT: the `contains` edges from every scoping construct are dropped — `@layer` (7,601), `@media` (2,921), `@container` (11) and `@supports` (1,376, and ZERO before its own fix). The scope symbol and the rules are all still published, so the graph can list both and never their membership. Caught by scope-conditions-and-custom-properties and layer-ordering-and-font-families, which pin `isLayerScope`/`isSupportsScope`/`isMediaScope` rows.

C6 REVERT: the `uses` edges from a `font-family` to a declared `@font-face` are dropped, along with the `list-style` -> `@counter-style` and `font-feature-settings` -> `@font-feature-values` twins. Measured pre-fix: 135 corpus files declare a `font-family`, 21 declare an `@font-face`, 344 family symbols published, and nothing connected them. Caught by layer-ordering-and-font-families' `isFontFamilyRef` row and declarations-the-corpus-never-uses' two `uses` rows.

C7 REVERT: every `var(--x)` read edge is dropped, which is the largest `references` class in the corpus at 13,218 edges, and with it the `@media (--narrow)` -> `--narrow` dependency. Every custom property stays published as a declaration with no reader. Caught by scope-conditions-and-custom-properties' `references` rows.

M59/#855 REVERT: every relationship loses its `line_number`, so 7,662 relationships that each point at a real line become unlocatable. No symbol or edge count changes, which is why this class is invisible to every gate that counts. Caught by M59 oracle-callsite and the CSS line oracle, which compare each edge's line against the source.

REVERT: every relationship loses `metadata.evidenceClass`, so a consumer can no longer tell a STRUCTURAL edge (containment, read from the tree) from a USAGE_CONTEXTUAL one (a `font-family` naming a family) or an IMPORT_BASED one (a `@import` target). The edges are all still there and all still correct, which is what makes the class worth a mutant: the defect is a claim becoming unverifiable rather than a count changing. Caught by the fixtures' `meta.evidenceClass` rows.

REVERT: the `errors` array is emptied, so a stylesheet the grammar could not read is reported as extracted cleanly. Error recovery is why a broken file still yields its surrounding rules, and that is correct — the defect is not the recovery but the COUNT, because every gate that does not read `errors` then sees a successful extraction of a file that failed. This is the class behind the lane's declared 25-file parse floor. Caught by the fixtures' `expectErrorCount` rows.

REVERT: the `isLayerScope`/`isMediaScope`/`isContainerScope`/`isSupportsScope`/`isScopeScope` markers are stripped from relationship metadata, so a consumer must re-parse a scope's NAME to learn what KIND of scope it is. Caught by the fixtures' `meta.isLayerScope` and `meta.isSupportsScope` rows.

REVERT: the markers that say which construct DECLARED a symbol are stripped. `@custom-media` publishes a bare `--narrow`, which is the same shape as a registered `@property` symbol and a rule-level custom property, so without `isCustomMediaDeclaration` / `isPropertyRegistration` / `isCounterStyleDeclaration` the three are indistinguishable in the graph. Two fields holding one value, or three fields holding none, is the same 'two truths' defect the complexity metric carried. Caught by declarations-the-corpus-never-uses' three marker rows and font-faces-and-registered-properties' `isPropertyRegistration` row.

S10 REVERT: two control-flow scopes with identical text collapse back into one symbol, so the second publishes nothing and the owner of everything inside it disappears. Identity by (kind, name) is CORRECT for a $variable — one thing assigned in several places — and wrong for a scope. Measured: two each_statements (L76, L266) in checkbox.scss, and 7 MISSING differential rows that were the analyzer losing information rather than the truth being wrong. Caught by identically-named-scopes-are-distinct, which pins BOTH the plain name and the #2 disambiguation.

S0 REVERT: a `$variable` is published once per ASSIGNMENT rather than once per name, so `$brand` assigned twice is two indistinguishable symbols and a `references` edge addresses one of them. The occurrence count is read from the SOURCE, because a result-derived count is always 1 after the fix and the transform would be a no-op — the exact bug the CSS lane's first identity mutant had, where it SURVIVED. Caught by variables-flags-and-identity's `expectSymbolCount` rows, which pin `$brand` and `$pad` at exactly 1 while the source assigns `$brand` twice.

S1 REVERT: `scssFlagDefault` and `scssFlagGlobal` stop being recorded, so a `!default` assignment is indistinguishable from an ordinary one. This is the first implementation's actual behaviour, for two stacked reasons: the walk used `namedChild` and the flag is two ANONYMOUS nodes, and the test looked for `!default` inside one node's text when the `!` and the word are separate nodes. 210 occurrences in the corpus. Caught by variables-flags-and-identity's two `meta.scssFlag*` rows.

S2 REVERT: an `@use '<mod>' as <ns>` namespace stops being published, so `map.merge(…)` has no endpoint and the binding the statement creates is invisible. This is the first implementation's actual behaviour, which excluded `sass:` modules as 'not the file's own' — a rule nobody wrote down. Caught by module-system-and-mixins' `{ name: 'map', kind: 'namespace' }` row.

S3 REVERT, and it ADDS rather than removes: `@return` emits `contains` from a function to ITSELF. A self-edge makes a relationship count look like evidence while connecting nothing, and it is syntactically well-formed — two real endpoints, nothing malformed — so it is the class a mutant suite catches better than a reading. This is what the first implementation did. Caught by functions-return-and-undeclared-uses' forbidRelationships row.

S4 REVERT: an `@include` of a mixin the file does not declare gets a `uses` edge to a name nothing publishes — the `global` phantom the CSS lane removed once, which a mixin from another stylesheet would bring straight back. Caught by functions-return-and-undeclared-uses' forbidRelationships row naming `not-declared-here`. The negative half is the half that distinguishes a lane from a faucet.

S5 REVERT: when no published symbol contains a statement, the edge is named after its own TARGET rather than skipped. That is the pre-fix behaviour and it produced three fabrications in one file — `uses button -> @mixin button`, `uses .btn -> .btn`, and a source that was raw declaration text. Ownership is now resolved by RANGE. Caught by control-flow-and-extend's `uses .card -> .btn` row, which the fallback turns into `.btn -> .btn` and trips the fixture's own forbidRelationship.

S6 REVERT: a `@mixin`/`@function` symbol loses its `parameters`, so a mixin's signature — the thing a call site is checked against — is absent while the symbol still looks whole. Caught by module-system-and-mixins' and functions-return-and-undeclared-uses' `expectParameters` rows.

S7 REVERT: `@extend` emits no edge, so a rule's inheritance by selector extension is invisible while both selectors still appear as symbols — the graph can list them and never their relation. Caught by control-flow-and-extend's `meta.isScssExtend` row.

S8 REVERT: `@use`/`@forward` stop producing imports, so a stylesheet's entire dependency on the Sass module system disappears from the result while its symbols all remain. Caught by module-system-and-mixins' `expectImports` rows, which pin both the module and the `as` namespace.

S9 REVERT: a control-flow scope stops recording its `@each` key/value, `@for` from/through and `@if` condition, so the scope symbol still looks whole while the only statement of intent the construct makes is gone. Caught by control-flow-and-extend's `meta.scssEachKey`/`scssEachValue`/`scssForFrom`/`scssForThrough` rows.

M59/#855 REVERT: every relationship loses its `line_number`. No symbol or edge COUNT changes, which is why this class is invisible to every gate that counts. Caught by M59 oracle-callsite and the SCSS line oracle.

REVERT: every relationship loses `metadata.evidenceClass`, so a consumer cannot tell a STRUCTURAL edge (`@extend`, containment) from a USAGE_CONTEXTUAL one (`@include`, a `$var` read) or an IMPORT_BASED one (`@use`). All the edges are still there and all still correct, which is what makes the class worth a mutant: the defect is a claim becoming unverifiable rather than a count changing. Caught by the fixtures' `meta.evidenceClass` rows.

REVERT: the `errors` array is emptied, so a stylesheet the grammar could not read is reported as extracted cleanly. This class is the reason the CSS lane needed an `error-recovery-is-reported` fixture at all: every CSS fixture originally asserted `expectErrorCount: 0`, which an EMPTY array satisfies, so the suite could not tell a clean parse from a swallowed failure. Caught by error-recovery-is-reported's `atLeast: 1`.

REVERT: the markers that say which SCSS construct DECLARED a symbol are stripped, so a `$variable` is indistinguishable from a registered `@property` and a control-flow `interface` from a `@supports` one. Caught by variables-flags-and-identity's `meta.isScssVariable` and control-flow-and-extend's `meta.isScssControlFlow` rows.

REVERT: every `uses` edge to a `@function` CALLED in a value disappears, so a declared function can never be reached from its call site and the graph cannot answer "who calls double". Found by the M12 independent hand audit of validation/m12/fixtures/scss/Theme.scss — 9 facts expected, 8 observed, recall 0.889, and the single false negative was this edge. It survived because a `@var` read on the line above was caught and a call on the line below was not: the two are the same class of claim and only one of them was implemented, so no count-based gate could see the gap.

REVERT: `metadata.scssRecoveredFromError` is stripped, so a claim the analyzer only recovered from inside a broken region becomes indistinguishable from one it read cleanly. The EDGES all survive this mutant, so every count-based gate passes; what is lost is the ability to tell a consumer which claims rest on a region the grammar could not read. The control for it is the same variable read twice in one fixture, once recovered and once clean.

REVERT: `metadata.isScssFunctionCall` is stripped, so a call to a user function is indistinguishable from an `@include` of a mixin — both are `uses`. A consumer could no longer tell a value-position call from a statement-position include, which is the difference between "this function is called" and "this block is included".

SOL-1 REVERT: the file-scope edge source goes back to the literal string `global`. That is the pre-wave shape in the sibling shell lanes verbatim (`relSource() || "global"`), and it is a fabrication by construction: `isIndexArtifactName` (src/ast/analysis-exclusions.ts:129) REJECTS `global` as a symbol name, so not one of those edges can ever resolve to a stored row — measured on that lane at the store as 4 of 7 relationships on a two-file project with `source_symbol_id = NULL`, and `bb_graph` on a method that IS called answering `callers: []`. Caught by the `global` forbid half of module-owner-sol1 and all-kinds-sol. Written generically off the `module` symbol, so it reverts whatever the fixture declares rather than a hard-coded file name.

SOL-2 REVERT: no relationship carries a `line_number` at all. The lane's headline number is `line=25750/25750 (100.00%)`, and it is a completeness check on the EMIT PATH rather than a quality score because the analyzer's single `addRel` helper refuses a non-positive line — an emit path that could produce a null could not be checked at all. Caught by every fixture's line pins.

SOL-2 REVERT, the second half: the edge identity loses the line, going back to `source|type|target`. Two call sites of one callee collapse to one row and the second site is swallowed — measured in a sibling lane as a `contains` edge pointing at a name the file does not declare, because `pushSymbol` dedupes the SYMBOL while the EDGE key did not. Caught by per-site-lines-sol2's two `calls` rows, which differ ONLY in `line_number`, and by its four `uses` rows for the same variable.

SOL-2 REVERT, the misattribution form: every edge takes the line of the ENCLOSING DECLARATION instead of the line its own name is written on. M60 #921's measured pre-fix shape, family-wide. Caught by per-site-lines-sol2: `calls one -> helper` is pinned at the CALL line while `contains Sites -> helper` is pinned at the DECLARATION line, so a transform that stamps the declaration line onto both fails the first and passes the second. Derived from the result's own symbol table — the first symbol of each owner is the enclosing declaration — rather than from a fixture name, and the `module` bucket is seeded by hand because the module carries no `ownerName`: the first version of this transform left every file-scope edge untouched and the MUTANT SURVIVED, which is the outcome that caught it.

SOL-13 REVERT: a method's outgoing edges are re-attributed to its OWNER, the contract. The pre-wave lane's shape, and the one PowerShell PS3 measured at the SURFACE as `bb_graph Start` returning `callers: []` and `callees: []` at once — a dead end in both directions, with the class absorbing every method's calls. Caught by per-site-lines-sol2's forbid row `calls Sites -> helper`. Written generically off the symbol table, so it reverts whatever the fixture declares.

SOL-13 REVERT, the containment half: a `variable` or `constant` symbol's containment edge goes back to the FILE. Measured on this lane while it was being built: the frame's owner was the contract, so `contains C -> ok` claimed a contract contains a local — and Solidity locals are strictly function-scoped, so the edge is simply false. Caught by call-shapes-sol9's `contains everyShape -> ok` at the FUNCTION and by module-owner-sol1's forbid row for a file-owned local. Derived generically: the TARGET of a `contains` edge is the declaration, so its kind is what says whether the edge is a local's or a member's. A first draft looked the kind up on the edge's SOURCE — which is the OWNER — found no variable-like symbol, changed nothing, and SURVIVED, i.e. it would have been reported as passing while testing nothing.

TIER REVERT: the evidence class is dropped from every edge. It is emitted CENTRALLY by one `evidenceClassFor` so no call site can forget it and none can drift, and the surface measure reads it from the analyzer's own emitter rather than recomputing it — which is why the tier histogram in `validation/m60/results/solidity-surface.json` cannot disagree with the emit path. Caught by every fixture's `meta.evidenceClass` pin, which is on almost every row.

TIER REVERT: every edge is stamped `structural`. The tiers are the graph engine's, and calling everything structural overstates the evidence — `overrides` locates its target by MATCHING a member name inside a base the tree only names, so it is `inferred`, and only `contains`/`extends`/`implements`/`exports`/`instantiates` are settled by the tree itself. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `overrides` row, which pins `meta.evidenceClass: inferred`, and by the `usage_contextual` pins on the call and use rows. Measured: the shipped histogram is 6,561 structural / 18,282 usage_contextual / 899 import_based / 8 inferred over 25,750 edges, so flattening it is a 25,750-row change that no count alone would notice.

THE MEASURED ZERO. `new_expression` nests its `user_defined_type` inside a `type_name` (grammar.js), so a direct-child read returned null and this lane emitted ZERO `instantiates` across a six-file probe set — while containing `A a = new A();`. The whole kind was absent and nothing reported it, because a metric that counts what exists cannot report a class that does not exist. Measured after the fix: 1 over the 389-file corpus, and the count is small enough that it needed a fixture. Caught by call-shapes-sol9's and all-kinds-sol's `instantiates` rows and `expectRelationshipCount`.

SOL-5 REVERT, the loss half: `implements` is dropped entirely. Solidity has ONE heritage construct and the tree does not say which kind each ancestor is, so a lane that only knew `extends` would have shipped 7 `implements` and 537 `extends` with nothing to notice. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `implements` row and its `equals: 1` count.

SOL-5 REVERT, the misattribution half — the more dangerous of the pair, because it loses nothing. Every `implements` edge is relabelled `extends`, so the total inheritance count is unchanged and only the KIND is wrong. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `forbidRelationships` row `extends Feed -> IFeed` and by its `implements equals 1` count; a fixture pinning only `implements -> IFeed` would pass under this mutant, which is why the forbid row and the count are both there.

SOL-11 REVERT: `overrides` is dropped. Solidity HAS the keyword, so this is not the PowerShell situation where the language offers nothing — the edge is dropped because the ANALYZER stopped resolving the target, which is the failure a keyword does not excuse. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `overrides` row and its `equals: 1` count. Measured context: 8 emitted over 389 files against 386 UNRESOLVED, because a base declared in another file yields no edge at all rather than a fabricated one — so this kind is small on purpose, and the count row is what stops 'small' from becoming 'missing'.

SOL-11 REVERT: instead of dropping an unresolvable override, FABRICATE one. For every method carrying `meta.hasOverrideSpecifier`, emit an `overrides` edge to the contract's first base even when that base is not declared in the file. This is the exact trap the rule exists to avoid: a fabricated target sits at ZERO `unknownTargets` — the metric asks whether a target MATCHES a symbol, and a name that matches nothing is no more detectable than one that matches something. The rejected shape is recorded as `metadata.overrideExternal: true` and a `references` edge instead. Caught by all-kinds-sol plus, on the corpus, by the surface measure's `overridesUnresolved: 386`.

SOL-12 REVERT: `exports` is dropped. Solidity has NO export construct, so nothing else in the lane would notice the kind is gone — a lane that silently omits one of the ontology's ten kinds has a hole in the matrix that no count reports. Caught by all-kinds-sol's four `exports` rows and module-owner-sol1's `equals: 7`.

SOL-12 REVERT, the WIDENING: every file-scope FUNCTION joins the export surface alongside the type declarations. `solc` emits an ABI and an abstraction for each contract, interface and library in a source unit and for nothing else — a free function lives in the unit's bytecode and contributes no ABI entry — so claiming it is an export asserts a surface the language does not define. Caught by module-owner-sol1's forbid row `exports … -> fileScopeFunction` and by its `exports equals 7` count, which a widened rule would make 8.

THE MEASURED ZERO, second instance. `yul_path`'s children are `yul_identifier`, not `identifier` — grammar.js declares `yul_identifier: $ => $.identifier`, an ALIAS, so the node type on the wire differs from the aliased one. A direct read of `identifier` children finds NONE of them, and this lane emitted zero Yul path reads over 2,640 `yul_path` corpus nodes while looking entirely healthy. Caught by yul-subset-sol's `isYulPathSegment` rows. Selecting on the METADATA rather than on the node type keeps the mutant generic and keeps it pointing at the behaviour rather than at the fixture.

SOL-9 REVERT, the measured total loss. The `isMemberCall` flag is stripped from every call, so the reserved-token rule stops exempting MEMBER calls and deletes them: `call`, `balance` and `delegatecall` are EVM opcode TOKENS and also members of Solidity's built-in types. Measured before the fix: `t.call{value: 1, gas: 100}("")` published NO edge at all, and the surface measure could not report the loss because the edge never existed to be counted. 3878 → 3810 calls is the whole difference and it was invisible until a fixture asked for the callee by name. Caught by call-shapes-sol9's `calls everyShape -> call` row and all-kinds-sol's `calls push -> latest` (`this.latest()`, a call through a global).

SOL-3 REVERT, the collision form: the synthesised getter takes the plain variable name instead of its external signature, so a `public uint256 balance` yields a method named `balance` beside the property named `balance`. Two rows that both resolve and that nobody can tell apart, and `bb_graph` would answer a question about which one. This is the shape the lane's FIRST draft tried to avoid by recording the getter in `metadata` and publishing nothing — a decision `parseFile` never received, because pool-worker drops the metadata object at the worker boundary. Caught by getter-sol3's `forbidSymbols` row for a method named `balance`.

SOL-3 REVERT, the omission form: no getter is published at all — which is what the first draft did, and what a reader of that draft would have called the shipped state. Solidity synthesises a getter for every `public` state variable (measured: 59 over the 389-file corpus) and a member surface missing them is missing functions the contract really has. Caught by getter-sol3's two `balance()`/`owner()` symbol rows, its two `contains` rows, and the forbid rows for `hidden()`/`secret()`, which is also what pins that visibility is read rather than 'every state variable'.

SOL-14 REVERT: declarations whose name the store refuses are declared anyway, and their containment edges emitted. pool-worker.ts's `UNIVERSAL` denylist says such names are 'never legitimate declarations in any language', which is false for Solidity's `self` (CrosschainLinked.sol:59) and `root` (MerkleTreeMock.sol:15) at this rev — measured as 2 unknown `contains` targets, because the store dropped both symbols while the edges survived. That is a shared-store over-reach rather than a grammar bug, and the file two blocks above that list already fixed the same class for JS globals. Caught by store-refusal-sol14's forbid rows for the symbols, the `contains` edges, and the getter link. Selected by the mirror set's membership, not by the two names, so a third name added to either list is covered automatically.

SOL-6 REVERT: the recovery rule is narrowed back to skipping an ERROR/MISSING node's DESCENDANTS, which is where it started and was not enough. On the fixture's line 7 the parser emits an ERROR covering only `is not ) valid solidity ( at`, so the tokens `this` and `all` are SIBLINGS of the ERROR node, outside its subtree: the pre-fix analyzer published a symbol named `all` and a type reference `this` — the parser's guess about garbage, stored as graph fact. The corpus is 0% damaged over all 389 production files, so NO corpus run can exercise this, which is exactly why the fixture forces an ERROR on purpose. Caught by recovery-regions-sol6's forbid rows for the symbol `all`, for `contains … -> all`, for `uses … -> this` and for `contains … -> this`, while its clean declarations on lines 5, 6 and 8 still have to survive.

SOL-11 REVERT, the whole defect in one edit: refuse to emit an `overrides` edge when the base is not declared in the same file. That is EXACTLY what the first version of this lane did, and it cost 414 true edges over the 389-file corpus while reporting itself clean — the JavaScript lane's `first-parent-guess` failure mode wearing a different language, since 15 sibling analyzers read an `overrideCompanion` hook that no production caller ever populates and every one of them would drop these edges the same way. Solidity needs no companion: the compiler rejects `override(X)` unless `X` declares the member, so the edge is the language's own invariant. Caught by external-override-sol11's `handle -> ILater` row, which this revert deletes outright.

SOL-11 REVERT, the honesty half: report an external-base `overrides` edge at the same 0.9 as an in-file verified one, keeping only the target and dropping the tier reasoning. Every COUNT stays identical and the edge is still correct, which is why this is the more dangerous half — a consumer cannot tell a member read from a declaration from one inferred from the compiler's rule. Caught by external-override-sol11's `confidenceMax: 0.75` and its `meta.reasonCode` / `meta.externalBase` pins.

SOL-11 REVERT, the refusal: emit an `overrides` edge for a bare `override` over TWO OR MORE header bases, picking the first. This fabricates 100 rows over the 389-file corpus and is the one shape where guessing is genuinely wrong rather than merely weak — Solidity 0.8.8+ requires an explicit list precisely when more than one base declares a member, so the keyword says one of them does and not which. Caught by external-override-sol11's TWO `ambiguous` forbid rows.

SOL-23 REVERT: stop reporting a `@param` that names a parameter the function does not have. The corpus reports ZERO of these across 389 files — entirely believable for OpenZeppelin, and indistinguishable from a checker that never fires. That indistinguishability is why natspec-check-sol23 forces the branch: without it, the zero would have been unfalsifiable. Caught by its `overDocumented` row.

SOL-23 REVERT, the over-claim direction: report `returnDocumentedWithoutReturn: false` on EVERY symbol, including the ones the check never ran on. This is the mirror defect and it is the more dangerous one, because it would make the corpus figure of zero mean NOTHING — a field that says 'checked and clean' on symbols that were never checked is worse than no field at all, and it is the same failure this repo calls a clean-looking zero for a thing that is not zero. Caught by natspec-check-sol23, whose `overDocumented` and `returnWithoutReturn` rows both require the flag to be present-and-false only where the check actually ran.

SOL-22 REVERT: stop reading the licence. Zero relationship, count or line changes — 389 files simply stop saying which licence they are under, and nothing in the repository can tell, because a payload-only revert is invisible to every count-based gate. That was the pre-SOL-22 state: 0 of 5,976 symbols carried a licence on a corpus where 389 of 389 files state one. Caught by licence-sol22's module row.

SOL-22 REVERT, the over-collection direction: scan the WHOLE file for the licence marker instead of only the first comment run. A licence buried on line 400 is a remark that happens to contain the word, and a file whose first comment is an ordinary remark would be reported as licensed when it declares nothing. Caught by licence-sol22, where the module row is MIT and every OTHER symbol is pinned `license: null` — so a rule that attached the file's licence to the declarations inside it fails on those rows.

SOL-21 REVERT: ignore `AnalyzeContext.projectIndex` entirely. That is the pre-SOL-21 behaviour, and it cost 507 undecided inheritance kinds and 1,487 unresolved call targets on the 389-file corpus — the whole point of adding an OPTIONAL field to a type fifteen sibling analyzers depend on. Caught by solidity-crossfile-gate's five `with-index` checks, which assert the kinds settle and the calls resolve.

SOL-21 REVERT, the honesty half: collapse `projectMemberCandidate` into `crossFileInheritedMember`, i.e. resolve a call whenever the index knows the name ANYWHERE rather than only through the OWNING contract's ancestors. This is the specific way the two grades could be confused, and it would convert 1,031 honest candidates into 1,031 confident facts — a Solidity `calls` edge carries no receiver type for a free function, so WHICH type is meant is undecidable. Caught by solidity-crossfile-gate's `candidate-is-not-a-resolution` check.

SOL-20 REVERT: stop publishing `qualified_calls`. 601 corpus symbols over 407 distinct qualified names stop saying which qualified calls they MAKE, and no relationship, count or line changes — so nothing but a gate can notice. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's `everything` row.

SOL-20 REVERT, the over-collection direction: include `abi.` and `type.` receivers. It ADDS rows rather than removing them, so no count-based gate would notice, and the effect is to put `abi.encode` in the same list as `Helpers.twice` — destroying the one distinction a reader of this field most needs, since a language namespace is not a call on an object. Caught by the same row, because the pinned list is exact.

SOL-19 REVERT: publish cross-file inheritance at confidence 1.0 with tier "structural", dropping `kindUnresolved`. No COUNT changes and no kind changes — the edge is still `extends` to the right target — which is why this needs its own mutant: the defect is purely that a guess was labelled a fact. 537 corpus rows carried it. A consumer weighting by evidence tier read an undecided KIND as structural, and one filtering `extends` to find contracts inherited a mis-typed base. Caught by inheritance-sol5's `confidenceMax: 0.95` and `meta.kindUnresolved` pin, plus its `confidenceMin: 0.99` forbid.

SOL-19 REVERT, a bug from the PREVIOUS commit: report a library member's `ownerKind` as "contract". `declareSymbol` maps BOTH `contract_declaration` and `library_declaration` to `SymbolKind.Class`, so deriving ownerKind from the SymbolKind cannot tell them apart. No gate caught this — the fixture that pinned it had been written against the buggy output. Found by reading contracts/utils/Strings.sol back. Caught by complexity-sol18's `fromLibrary` row, now pinned as `library`.

SOL-18 REVERT: report complexity 1 for every symbol. This is not a hypothetical shape — it is EXACTLY what the lane published for its whole life, because `pool-worker` defaults to `s.complexity || s.metadata?.complexity || 1` and the analyzer set neither, so the field was populated corpus-wide with a constant that reads as a measurement. Caught by complexity-sol18's seven `complexity` pins.

SOL-18 REVERT, the attribution half: count branches over the whole FILE rather than per frame, so every function in a file inherits the file's branch total. It is the natural wrong implementation — the file-level cyclomatic count already exists and is computed in the same loop — and it would pass any fixture whose file has one branchy function. Caught by complexity-sol18: `straight` is 1 and `twoBranches` is 3 in the SAME file, so a file-wide count cannot satisfy both.

SOL-18 REVERT: report every `ownerKind` as "contract". The plausible-looking wrong answer: an interface's members and a library's members both look like members of something, and 'contract' is the default kind for a type declaration. Caught by complexity-sol18's `ownerKind: "interface"` on `IThing.external1`.

SOL-16 REVERT: stop publishing `docstring`. No relationship, count or line changes at all — 2,779 of 5,976 symbols simply stop carrying their documentation, and `brain_symbol.docstring` goes back to NULL for every Solidity symbol in the index. A payload-only revert is invisible to every count-based gate in the repository, which is why it needs one of its own. Caught by natspec-sol16's five `docstring` pins.

SOL-16 REVERT, the bug the fixture was written for: attach documentation PER COMMENT instead of per RUN, so only the LAST comment of a run survives. This is not hypothetical — it was the first implementation, and it published `library Docs` as documented by `@author Someone` while silently dropping the `@title` and `@notice` above it, i.e. two lines kept out of every three, on every documented declaration in the corpus. Caught by natspec-sol16's exact `docstring` for `Docs` and `SLOT`.

SOL-16 REVERT, the second bug the fixture was written for: do not clear the run anchor after a flush, so a TRAILING comment run at the end of a parent reuses the previous declaration as its target. On natspec-sol16 that published the file's closing remark as part of `IThing`'s docstring — the precise opposite of what a trailing remark is. Modelled from the SOURCE, because the harness passes `content` and a fixture-phrase key would never fire. Caught by natspec-sol16's exact `docstring` for `IThing`. (The mutant body uses a small regex; the ZERO-REGEX gate scopes the ANALYZER, and a revert written against the fixture's own text would be the weaker instrument.)

SOL-17 REVERT: stop publishing applied modifiers on the `decorators` field. 188 corpus symbols over 40 distinct modifier names stop carrying them; no relationship changes, because the `calls` edge for an applied modifier is emitted by the `modifier_invocation` case and is untouched. Caught by modifiers-sol17's four `decorators` pins.

SOL-17 REVERT, the over-collection direction: publish EVERY modifier declared anywhere in the file as a decorator on EVERY function. This is the failure mode of reading modifiers from the enclosing contract instead of from the function's own header, and it is the reason modifiers-sol17 pins `single` as exactly `["onlyOwner"]` — `single` applies one modifier while three are in scope, so this turn would make the fixture fail rather than quietly widen. Caught by modifiers-sol17's `single` and `paired` pins.

SOL-16's audit find: revert the `using_alias` case to looking for DIRECT `identifier` children. The grammar nests the name as `using_alias (user_defined_type (identifier)) (user_definable_operator)`, so the direct-child search is empty for every input and the branch had NEVER fired — 4 `using_alias` nodes in the corpus, all in contracts/account/utils/draft-ERC7579Utils.sol, and 0 edges. Found by a per-case emit census, the same signature as the `revert_statement` dead branch.

SOL-15 REVERT, the payload half: strip `calleeKind` from every `calls` edge. No COUNT changes — 4,331 edges stay 4,331 and every kind's edge count stays put — so nothing but the gate can notice. What is lost is the one field that says whether a callee is a symbol at all, and with it the difference between `abi.encode` (a language namespace), a custom error, and a member declared in another file. That difference is the whole content of the 1,849-row unresolved figure. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's four `meta.calleeKind` pins.

SOL-15 REVERT, the RULE half: report every call as `external`. This is the classifier as it behaves when resolution never runs — and it is what the lane effectively shipped before SOL-15, except that the field did not exist then, so a consumer could not even tell resolution had been skipped. With the field present and flat, the four kinds collapse to one and every count stays identical. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's three `meta.calleeKind` forbids — which is where the closure-order bug WOULD have been caught, had the fixture existed when the bug was written.

SOL-15 REVERT, the never-fired branch: revert the `revert_statement` case to its original form, which tested `node.namedChild(0).type === "identifier"` and was therefore FALSE for every possible input, because the grammar puts an `expression` wrapper there for `revert Boom(1)`, `revert Solo` and `revert("x")` alike. That is 453 custom-error call edges over the 389-file corpus that this lane did not emit AT ALL, and no gate noticed — the kind had a case in the source, so it read as covered. Caught by call-resolution-sol15's `boom -> Boom` row and its `errorRevert` forbid.

IMPORT REVERT, the annotation half. `imports` is not a relationship kind in this product: an import is a `references` edge carrying `metadata.import: true` (the settled convention, the same reason PowerShell PS-7 used it), so the ANNOTATION is what distinguishes an import from any other reference. Stripping it leaves the edge type intact and the meaning gone — 899 edges over the 389-file corpus would stop being imports while every count stayed identical. Caught by all-kinds-sol's two import rows' `meta.import` pins and its `references equals 4`.

IMPORT REVERT, the MEASURED ZERO. `import * as Utils from "./Utils.sol"` produced NO edge while a braced import produced one per name — two import statements yielded one edge, because the reader only looked for a plain import name and the namespace form has only an ALIAS. The edge that was missing is the one naming the local binding, the only name the importing file can use. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `references … -> Utils` row and its `expectImports`, and by the `references equals 4` count, which a rule that handled only two of the three import forms would make 3.

F9 REVERT: the plausible-name gate stops refusing a target containing a path separator, so a bare `import "./Bare.sol";` grows a `references` edge naming the path. That edge can never resolve to a stored symbol, and — the reason F9 exists — it would sit at ZERO `unknownTargets` for exactly as long as it existed, because the metric asks whether a target MATCHES a symbol and a name matching nothing is no more detectable than a name matching something. Measured on a sibling lane: malformed here-string targets sat at 0 unknown indefinitely. The correct state is that a bare import binds no name and so contributes an `imports` payload row and no edge. Caught by all-kinds-sol's `forbidRelationships` row naming the path. The first draft of this transform went the WRONG WAY — it removed path-targeting edges, which is the opposite of a revert of the gate and therefore a no-op, because the gate working means there are none to remove. A revert has to ADD what the gate suppresses.

JUL-1 REVERT: a qualified callee collapses to its LAST SEGMENT, which is what the analyzer did before `fieldPath` kept the whole path. Measured over 400 corpus files: 1,352 bare segments appear behind a qualified path and 72 of them are reachable by MORE THAN ONE distinct path — `parse` alone is `Meta.parse`, `Base.parse`, `TOML.parse` and `Dates.parse`, and `bitcast` is `Base.bitcast`, `Core.bitcast` and `Intrinsics.bitcast`. Collapsing fuses unrelated functions into one node, and a fused node makes every edge into and out of it a statement about the wrong function. Caught by the `Base.show` symbol and by modules-and-scope.

JUL-2 REVERT: relationships sourced from the file scope are dropped, which is the pre-`GLOBAL_SCOPE` shape (`if (scope)` guarding every emit). Measured over 295 corpus files: 71.9% of Julia files have NO module block, and 46 of those emitted ZERO call edges while holding 8,478 `call_expression`s between them — a script calling a dozen functions indexed as a file containing nothing. Caught by the `global -calls-> println` assertion in modules-and-scope.

JUL-3 REVERT: `activeScope` is never restored on an exit frame, so it DRIFTS FORWARD and the last declaration to advance it owns every later sibling. Reverted here by re-attributing every relationship to the last symbol declared at or before its line — which is precisely the behaviour the missing restore produced. On the fixture it moves `describe`'s body onto `Area`, the previous function: `Area -calls-> string@17`, `Area -calls-> typeof@17`. Caught by dispatch-and-hierarchy's `Geom -contains-> describe` and by the `describe` symbol's ownership.

JUL-4 REVERT: a declaration's own left-hand side is walked as an invocation, so every short-form function calls itself — `f(x) = …` DEFINES f and Julia does not invoke it there. Measured across the 200-file corpus: 2,502 such false self-calls, the largest single source of wrong edges in the lane. Caught by the `calls` forbids on Area, scaled and perimeter in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-5 REVERT: `export X` fabricates a `function` symbol for X. An export MARKS a binding, it does not declare one, and Julia allows the export to precede the declaration. Dedup could not merge it because its key is `kind:owner:name` and the kinds differed, so a real `class:Circle` sat beside a second, wrongly-kinded `Circle`. Caught by the `Circle`/`Square` symbol kinds in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-6 REVERT: a type's OWN `type_head` is read as a reference, so every struct published a reference to itself — `Shapes -references-> Circle`, a declaration stating itself. The head names the type being declared. Caught by nothing in isolation (a self-reference is a weak signal), which is why this mutant is kept: it is the shape the ancestor-aware guard in `withinTypeHead` exists to prevent, and the guard's parent-only version passed the non-generic fixture case while missing `Circle{T} <: Shape`.

JUL-7 REVERT: the walk descends into a struct's type parameters, so `struct Circle{T<:Real} <: Shape` published `Circle <: Real`. `T<:Real` bounds a PARAMETER; it says nothing about Circle's supertype. A parameter list is a wall, not a road. Caught by the `Circle -extends-> Shape` and `Square -extends-> Shape` assertions — a fabricated `extends Real` leaves those intact, so the defect is visible as an EXTRA edge rather than a missing one.

JUL-8 REVERT: every `extends` edge is dropped, reproducing the state where `<:` was invisible because `binary_expression`'s operator is a NAMED child at index 1 — so `pos(node,1)` returned the operator instead of the right operand and an anonymous-child scan found nothing. Zero `extends` over a corpus with thousands, on files that parse with zero ERROR nodes. Caught by both `extends` assertions in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-9 REVERT: a type is published under its SUPERTYPE's name. `struct Circle{T<:Real} <: Shape` makes the head a `binary_expression` whose first identifier anywhere in the subtree is `Shape`, so one `class:Shape` carried `contains -> radius` and the real `Circle` was absent — name and supertype swapped by the same mistake. Caught by the `Circle` and `Square` class symbols in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-10 REVERT: a call reached through `ccall`/`@ccall` is marked as a Julia binding call. The call is real; the claim that its target is a JULIA FUNCTION is not — `strlen` and `jl_issorted` are C symbols that do not exist in Julia's namespace. Caught by all three `meta.isForeignCall` assertions in macros-and-foreign.

JUL-11 REVERT: a generic method's declaration is dropped. `function scaled{T<:Real}(s, k)` has callee children `parametrized_type_expression` + `argument_list`, which `calleeName` did not handle, so Julia's most characteristic construct — a parametric method — was invisible to the lane whose job is to notice that. Caught by the `scaled` symbol in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

JUL-12 REVERT: a function carrying a RETURN-TYPE annotation publishes under the return type. `function scaled{T<:Real}(s::Shape, k::T)::Float64` makes the signature a `typed_expression` whose siblings are the callable and the return type, so an identifier scan found `Float64` first and `scaled` was lost. Third instance of the same class in this lane: scan for a name before unwrapping the wrapper around it. Caught by the `scaled` symbol and `Geom -contains-> scaled`.

JUL-13 REVERT: `f(x)::T = …` is not recognised as a declaration. A return-type annotation puts a `typed_expression` on the assignment's left, so the short-form handler's `call_expression` test failed. `x::Int = 5` is also a `typed_expression`, so the wrapper is unwrapped only when it wraps a CALL. Caught by the `perimeter` symbol in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

REVERT: `declaredTypes` is filled DURING the walk, so a call to a type declared LATER in the file is a plain `calls` instead of `instantiates`. The pre-fix code consulted the set mid-walk; the comment on the variable already claimed the opposite ('consulted afterwards, so a type declared later in the file still counts'), which is why it survived review — the code said one thing and the comment the other, and the comment was believed. Found by the F5 `instantiates` oracle: `Compiler/test/EAUtils.jl` calls `GetEscapeCache()` on line 52 and declares it on line 90. Reverted generically by demoting every `instantiates` edge whose line precedes the type's own declaration.

REVERT: a `where` clause's upper bound is a subtype edge from the type PARAMETER, and the emit was guarded by `scope` even though `scope` is not that edge's source. Copy-pasted from the `contains` cases, where the scope IS the source and the guard is the point — so it suppressed a valid edge wherever the bound appeared at FILE SCOPE, which is 71.9% of Julia files. Found by the F5 `extends` oracle: `base/rational.jl` publishes `T extends AbstractFloat` and `base/hashing.jl` `UTF8Units extends AbstractString`, neither of which the analyzer had. Reverted by dropping the `isWhereBound` edges, which is the pre-fix observable.

REVERT: the `where`-bound scan looks only at the where_expression's DIRECT children, so the braced spelling `where {T<:Real}` is missed while the bare `where T<:Real` is found. Julia people write the braced form, so the common shape produced no `T extends Real` at all. Found because this mutant SURVIVED its first form: a fixture whose `where` bound was invisible to the analyzer could not catch the defect that hid it, and a fixture and an analyzer agreeing on nothing is not a test. Caught by the `T extends Real` assertion in dispatch-and-hierarchy.

PRE-FIX: `Public Sub New()` has no `name` field -- the grammar lexes `New` as an anonymous token -- so `declaredName` returned empty and the 'declaration without a name' guard RETURNED before the naming contract was reached. The contract existed and was dead code: 12,549 symbols across 435 files contained ZERO constructors. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping every Constructor symbol and the containment edge into it, which is exactly the state that guard produced. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects two `constructor` symbols and two `contains -> constructor` edges.

PRE-FIX: containment was emitted per visitor, and the visitors for nested TYPES emitted none. A nested type therefore carried `ownerName` on its symbol and NO `contains` edge into it -- the owner recorded and then unreachable, so containment navigation stopped at the enclosing class. Found by the F5 differential and not by a fixture: 48 `contains Namespace -> Class` rows and every nested-type edge were invisible to a symbol count. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping the `contains` edge into any type whose owner is itself a symbol of this file, which is precisely the set the per-visitor dispatch failed to cover. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `contains Box -> Kind` and the enum members under it.

PRE-FIX: a construction IS a call, and the grammar spells it with one of TWO node types -- `New Box()` is an `invocation_expression`, but `New Box(1, 2)` is an `array_creation_expression` with a `type` field and no `function` field. Keying on the invocation alone dropped every call edge for a construction WITH ARGUMENTS: 15,577 occurrences across 1,718 of the corpus's 2,660 files. Recorded for a second reason: the F5 differential reported 100 % WITH THIS DEFECT PRESENT, because the oracle keyed on `invocation_expression` too. Two implementations that share an assumption are one implementation with a witness -- divergence has to cover the assumptions, not only the traversal. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping every `calls` edge the analyzer itself marked `constructed` with a node type other than `object_creation_expression`, read off the edge's own metadata so the mutant cannot silently stop matching when the fixture changes. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `calls Build -> Box` at line 55.

The pre-fix FK test matched ANY `object_reference` child of a `column_definition`, so a user-defined column TYPE (also an object_reference) was indistinguishable from a `REFERENCES` target: `CREATE TABLE t (b my_schema.my_type)` published `references t -> my_type` and the "Foreign Key Constraints" pattern — one phantom FK per custom-typed column, measured corpus-wide. Simulated as a faithful REVERT of the fix: a column that declares a type and declares NO reference is exactly the case the fix corrected, so the pre-fix state is re-derived from the fixed result by giving that column a reference equal to the type's last segment, plus the edge and the pattern the pre-fix code added. Caught by sql/sqld1-column-types, whose forbidRelationships name `references d1_columns->my_type` and `-> my_schema`.

The pre-fix parameter-type accessor matched `keyword_*` before the type, and a parameter MODE is a keyword, so `IN a integer` published `{ name: "a", type: "IN" }` — the mode recorded as the type for every mode-prefixed argument. The fixed result carries the mode in `direction` and the real type in `type`, so the pre-fix state is re-derived by copying the mode into `type`. Caught by sql/sqld3-routine-signature, whose forbidParameters pin `types: ["IN","OUT","INOUT"]`.

The pre-fix trigger read the first three `object_reference`s ANYWHERE in the subtree, and a `WHEN (old.a <> new.a)` clause contributes two more (old/new are object_references in this grammar) — so `… WHEN (old.a <> new.a) EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_it()` published `calls tg->old`, a call edge into a PL/pgSQL pseudo-variable, instead of `calls tg->audit_it`. The fixed result carries the CORRECT actionFunction; the trigger's own source line is what distinguishes a WHEN-bearing trigger, and the harness passes the source for exactly this. Faithful revert: for a trigger whose statement contains a WHEN clause, set actionFunction to `old` and repoint the calls edge. Caught by sql/sqld2-trigger-when, whose forbidRelationships name `calls d2_when->old` and `-> new`.

The pre-fix code had no reserved-word guard, so error recovery turned SQL keywords and role names into graph nodes: 49 keyword-target edges measured over 441 corpus files — `calls global->USING`, `uses global->WITH`, `calls get_brand_network_stats->FILTER` — and from `REVOKE … FROM joe` a bare `uses global->joe`, a ROLE published as a table. With GRANT/REVOKE now parsing, the honest place to re-inject the pre-fix state is the construct that USED to be an ERROR: a REVOKE whose grantee the old code read out of a `from` clause. Faithful: for a source with `REVOKE … FROM <role>`, emit the `uses global-><role>` edge the pre-fix parser produced. Caught by sql/sqld4-statement-dispatch, whose forbidRelationships name `uses global->some_role`.

The pre-fix CTE guard matched on the BARE LEAF, so a QUALIFIED reference whose leaf collided with a CTE name was suppressed with it: `WITH a AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM a JOIN s.a ON true` emitted NO relationship at all — both of the file's edges vanished on a real table. The fixed result HAS the qualified edge (the pattern proves a CTE is in play); the pre-fix state is its absence. Faithful: drop the `uses` edge from global to any target, in a source that declares a CTE. Caught by sql/sqld5-quoted-and-cte, whose `uses global->d5_cte` expect row fails when the edge is gone.

The pre-fix range helper emitted 0-BASED columns. The engine's own ParseError range (engine.ts:1180) and every other analyzer that builds a range use `startPosition.column + 1`, so SQL was the only 0-based range in the tree and all four column fields of EVERY SQL symbol were off by one, corpus-wide. Simulated generically: every symbol's range and every relationship's site line loses the 1-based base. Caught by sql/sqld8-range-and-ids, whose expectSymbolRanges pin startColumn 3 / endColumn 5 for two columns.

The pre-fix `id` was `parentId ?? name`, so two top-level entities sharing a bare name collided: `CREATE TABLE a.t` and `CREATE TABLE b.t` both got id `t` (measured ids ["t","t"]). Duplicate ids silently drop nodes from id-keyed graph consumers and conflate two distinct declarations — the RSD3 class. Simulated generically: every top-level symbol's id is rewritten to its bare name, so same-named top-level declarations collide. Caught by sql/sqld8-range-and-ids, whose expectUniqueIds name `d8_samename` (three declarations, one bare name).

The pre-fix `COMMENT ON COLUMN t.c` published a dependency on the COLUMN. The grammar nests a qualified column reference's table as a CHILD object_reference (`object_reference "t.c" > object_reference "t" + identifier "c"`), so a flat identifier walk saw only `c` and resolved the reference to the column — measured on database/migrations/20260702_inventory_categories_nutrition_translations.sql, which published `uses global->calories` for `COMMENT ON COLUMN business_inventory_items.calories`. The first version of the FIX took parts[0] and edged the SCHEMA instead, which the fixture's forbid row catches; the ruled answer is the second-to-last segment. The edge carries `metadata.column` precisely so the pre-fix target is reconstructable from the result, and this mutant is that reconstruction: a documented-column edge retargeted to the column it documents. Caught by sql/sqld10-qualified-and-recovery, whose forbidRelationships name `references global->total`, `-> qty` and `-> app`.

The pre-fix ALTER reader took the FIRST `add_column` descendant, but the grammar gives each added column its own `add_column` SIBLING rather than one comma list — so `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a int, ADD COLUMN b text, ADD COLUMN c numeric(6,2)` published `a` and dropped `b` and `c`. Measured on the corpus: a five-column `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` migration published one of its five. Simulated as a revert: keep only the FIRST added column of each table and drop the rest, which is exactly the pre-fix output. Caught by sql/sqld10-qualified-and-recovery, whose expectSymbols and expectSymbolCount name all three added columns.

The declaration sweep stopped descending once it met a declaration node, so a declaration NESTED INSIDE another declaration was unreachable. That is the ordinary shape after error recovery buries a statement: on database/schema.sql a function body the grammar could not finish swallows the rest of the file, and the CREATE TABLE nodes after it are children of that function's `function_body`. Measured on that file alone: 401 of its 3,557 symbols — 1,980 published before the fix, 3,557 after — and the corpus's most-referenced tables (business_profiles, business_content, business_locations) were among the casualties. The analyzer REPORTS the count as `ambiguity.sweepDeclarationsRecovered`, which is what makes the pre-fix state reconstructable: this mutant drops exactly the declarations the sweep alone contributed, which is what the old sweep's `continue` produced. Caught by sql/sqld10-qualified-and-recovery, whose `after_damage` symbol exists only if the sweep descends through the declaration.

The pre-fix analyzer returned `errors: []` UNCONDITIONALLY, so a file it could not parse at all read as a clean 0 symbols / 0 relationships / 0 errors. Every gate that calls `analyzer.analyze` directly — the fixture lane, this mutation harness, the m12 differential — saw a successful analysis of a total failure, and the m12 differential's error channel was vacuous for sql. Simulated generically: the analyzer's own `errors` array is emptied, keeping the result otherwise identical. Caught by sql/sqld7-error-honesty, whose expectErrors pin a warning and whose expectSymbols pin the declarations that survive beside the damaged lines — a suppression fix passes the first and fails nothing, so the second is what stops over-correction.

The pre-fix `statement` branch forwarded only `isDeclaration()` types and otherwise tested the children for a query shape, then RETURNED — so a statement holding anything else never reached the switch below it. Measured dead arms: set_statement, reset_statement and comment_statement (all three ARE produced by the pinned grammar, so "Session Configuration" and "SQL Documentation" could never fire), and merge/truncate, whose grammar rules are HIDDEN so the keywords inline into `statement` and an arm keyed on the node type can never run. Simulated generically: the patterns and edges those arms are the sole producers of are removed, and the merge/truncate/grant edges go with them. Caught by sql/sqld4-statement-dispatch, whose expectPatterns name all five.

H1 regression: the path reader is gated on `node.type === "expression"`, so the grammar's `operation -> binary_operation` operand run is never recognised. Every reference inside a comparison or arithmetic expression is dropped (758 corpus attributes; `is_restored = var.db_snapshot_identifier != null` published nothing). Reverted generically: a reference whose target line is not the line of any attribute, and which is a two-segment path, is removed — i.e. only the operands the gate could reach survive.

H8 regression: the `object_elem` key exclusion is read by pairing a NAMED-child index with `fieldNameForChild` (which indexes over ALL children), so a key that has any token before it is walked as a reference. Reverted generically: a two-segment path whose base is a declared variable and whose head matches an object key in the source becomes an edge. hcl/object-key-not-reference pins `(var.d) = var.e` and `(format("%s", var.g)) = var.h`, whose keys must stay silent.

H7 regression: a `dynamic` block's loop local is not tracked, so `iterator = r` + `r.cidr` (and the label-default form `dynamic "egress"` + `egress.cidr`) publish false references to a symbol that does not exist. Reverted generically: any two-segment path whose base is the name of a loop binding declared in the source becomes an edge. hcl/dynamic-iterator-scope pins r.cidr, r.port and egress.cidr silent.

H7b regression: a `dynamic` block's loop local is bound by THAT block and dies with it, but the first version of the H7 fix bound it for the whole ENCLOSING subtree. A resource carrying `dynamic "assume_role"` and, later, `dynamic "vpc"` then silenced its own `vpc.*` reads. Measured over the 9,079-file corpus as 247 lost references, 165 of them `assume_role.value` in tf-aws-components' provider files alone. Reverted generically: every reference whose base is the LABEL of a `dynamic` block in the same file is dropped, which is the subtree-wide binding. hcl/dynamic-sibling-scope pins vpc.value silent (it is that block's own local) AND vpc.value absent as a loss, via the `data.aws_subnet.by_id` edge on the same line.

Builtins-published-as-project-symbols regression: `count`/`each`/`self`/`path`/`terraform` resolve to nothing in the index because no file can declare them, so they are the `uses` class (global namespace, per real-sql-analyzer.ts:1569). Publishing them as `references` asserted a declaration that does not exist — 2,029 edges over 9,079 files, led by path.module (506), each.key (325), each.value (285), count.index (214). Reverted generically: every `uses` edge is relabelled `references`. hcl/builtin-vs-project-reference forbids that for all six.

The INVERSE of the mutant above, and the reason the class boundary is worth pinning in both directions: a project address published as `uses` claims it is a global, which demotes a real declaration out of the reference graph and out of every consumer that follows `references`. Reverted generically: every `references` edge whose target root is a project root is relabelled `uses`. hcl/builtin-vs-project-reference forbids this for var/data/local.

Finding G1 (the grammar repair's half that lives in the ANALYZER's reach). A processing instruction's content is the `_pi_content` external token, which the wired grammar used to fail to produce unless the byte after `?>` was a newline, so a content-bearing PI became an ERROR node the analyzer could not dispatch. Reverted generically: a `module` symbol the analyzer recorded with `isProcessingInstruction` and that the SOURCE spells with content between its target and `?>` is dropped, together with its edge. The pre-repair shape is not a missing symbol here — the analyzer is unchanged and the GRAMMAR is what changed — so the mutant models the observable consequence: the PI the grammar can no longer produce. Pinned by xml/pi-and-stylesheet, whose `<?catalog-processing build="12"?>` is content-bearing; the pre-existing M12 fixture used `<?catalog-processing?>`, the one spelling the broken grammar handled.

Finding G2, and the worst class in the lane: a PUBLISHED LIE rather than a missing fact. `<![INCLUDE[<!ELEMENT a EMPTY>]]>` inside an internal subset made the pre-repair grammar wrap the `doctypedecl` in an ERROR; the parser then took a LATER `Name` as the DTD's name, and the position-blind `findDirectChild(node, "Name")` published a Type symbol literally named `INCLUDE` with a `contains` edge from it. Reverted generically: the analyzer's own DTD-position guard is removed, so the FIRST `Name` beneath a `doctypedecl` becomes the DTD's name — which is the pre-fix behaviour verbatim, because the position-blind lookup and the recovery shape together produced exactly that. Pinned by xml/conditional-section, which forbids a symbol named `INCLUDE` and an edge from one.

Finding X1, the largest recall hole in the lane. In a schema language a construct's DECLARED NAME is the value of its `name` attribute, so the pre-fix analyzer published the TAG and the corpus filed every XSD type under one of six names — `xsd:element` alone appeared 5,914 times — while `bb_search("EntryType")` returned nothing. Measured: 1,197 of 26,578 in-vocabulary declarations published under their declared name, recall 0.045; after the fix, 18,490, recall 0.696, with the 29,196 out-of-vocabulary `name` attributes left untouched. Reverted generically: every symbol the analyzer recorded with `isVocabDeclaration` is relabelled to its `tagName` and the edges that name it are retargeted, which is the pre-fix reading exactly. Pinned by xml/declared-name-xsd.

The M60.R10 class, inverted. A `references` edge's target must be the NAME a declaration carries — the local part — because that is what resolves in the graph. Publishing the written value `tns:CatalogType` puts a value where a name belongs, and no declaration anywhere carries it, so every consumer following the edge finds nothing. Reverted generically: every reference edge the analyzer recorded as `attribute_qname_reference` is retargeted to the written `qname` from its own metadata. Pinned by xml/declared-name-xsd and xml/type-graph, which both forbid a colon-bearing target.

Finding L1 (M59.A7 / #825). The edge's target is the PATH, so the edge's line is the line the path is written on. The pre-fix code passed the whole `ExternalID` node, so `<!DOCTYPE hibernate-mapping PUBLIC 
 	"…/…-pubid"
 	"…/…-3.0.dtd">` pointed the edge at line 2, the `PUBLIC` keyword's line — the line of no name in the edge. Measured on the corpus: 8 of the first 60 files wrong, every multi-line DOCTYPE. Reverted generically: every `imports` edge whose metadata says it came from an external ID is moved to the line of the OWNING declaration's start, which is where the keyword is. Pinned by xml/dtd-declarations, which asserts `shared -> shared.dtd` on 3 while the doctypedecl opens on 2, and by the M12 contract probe's `the external-ID edge points at the PATH's line` check.

The no-unknown-symbols rule for `references`. The post-fix analyzer emits a reference only when the target RESOLVES in this document or is a known specification built-in, because a value naming nothing the document declares would put a name in the graph that no file supports. Reverted generically: every attribute value that is lexically a QName becomes a reference, resolvable or not — which is the pre-fix measurement (7,039 distinct QName values, recall 0.001, and 25,381 declarations whose name the analyzer did not resolve). Pinned by xml/type-graph, whose forbid list refuses a reference to an undeclared name, and by the M12 probe's `a call to a template the document does not declare is refused`.

Finding X3. Edge identity is `source|type|target`, so N declarations of one pair necessarily share one edge — a property of the schema, and the differential measures it separately for that reason. What was a defect is that the analyzer let the first line stand for all of them: 544,304 declaration occurrences collapsed onto 42,901 edges, and every occurrence after the first was unreachable with nothing recording it. Reverted generically: the collapse bookkeeping is undone — `occurrences` and `lines` are deleted and the edge's line is left wherever the walk first put it, so a later declaration's EARLIER line (a DTD content model read after the element it names) is lost. Pinned by xml/edge-collapse, which asserts occurrences 3 and lines [3,4,5], and by xml/dtd-declarations, whose `catalog -> entry` edge is one edge for two writings with the line at the DECLARATION site.

Finding X4.
