The pre-fix lane published 27,228 symbols from 177 files it simultaneously reported as erroneous, with nothing on any of them saying so; the shipped check `malformed XML creates no recovery symbols` was a FIXTURE ACCIDENT (an unterminated element yields no `element` node to publish, so the check passed for a reason unrelated to the analyzer's policy). The fix LABELS rather than suppresses, because a 90 %-parseable vendor template is thousands of real declarations and must stay visible. Reverted generically: the `syntaxErrors` label is stripped from every symbol and edge, which is the pre-fix reading — the symbols are still published, which is exactly the dishonest state. Pinned by xml/recovery-labelling, whose every expectation carries the label.

The `calls` ruling, reverted: HCL declares no function, class or type of any kind (0 of its 64 node types), and across 12,977 `function_call` nodes in 9,079 files not ONE callee resolves to a declared symbol — the 5 distinct apparent matches are provable name collisions with Terraform globals (length, file, timestamp, lower) and with a type keyword (`object`, in `type = object({…})` beside a declared `output` block literally named object — the quotes are elided here because a raw quote would terminate this description string. So a `calls` edge is 100% dangling, and the house precedent suppresses it (java/groovy carry explicit builtin filters for println/printf). Reverted generically: function-call callee names taken from the source are published as `calls` edges from every block.

H4 regression: a label-less `data {}` / `resource "x" {}` derives its name from `labels.join(".")` over ZERO labels, which is the empty string, so the symbol is nameless and its child attribute is left with an empty scope and no owner. Reverted generically: any block symbol with no labels loses its name. hcl/sibling-identity pins `data` at line 22 named `data`, never empty.

H3 regression: sibling blocks sharing a leaf name collapse onto one identity, so `contains` edges dedupe away all but the first. Measured pre-fix: 6897 duplicate pairs over 1323 distinct keys (worst: `parameter` at 420, waypoint's label-less repeats; `removed` 97, `moved` 82, `locals` 65, provider aliases 30). Reverted generically: every disambiguated sibling name is rewritten back to its bare address, reproducing the collision and the edge collapse. hcl/sibling-identity pins locals/locals#2/locals#3 and lifecycle/lifecycle#2 as distinct.

H2 regression (M59.A7 #825): relationships carry no line. Measured pre-fix through the production entry: 0 of 138,353 lined, from the product's side as well as the analyzer's — parallel-indexer.ts (:2789, :4393) persists only `rel.line_number` and graph.ts (:526) surfaces only that field, so an edge under any other spelling is stored NULL. Reverted generically: `line_number` is removed from every relationship, which is exactly the pre-fix shape.

H11 regression: the document root takes the bare file stem, so a file whose stem equals a top-level block's Terraform address gives the document and the block one identity. Measured: 308 corpus sites (`moved.tf` holding `moved {}` at 13, `removed` 9, `worker` 3, `locals` 3, `import` 3). Reverted generically: any top-level block whose address equals the root name is renamed back to that address. hcl/sibling-identity pins the root as `sibling-identity` and its blocks as distinct from it.

H5 regression: the attribute branch is guarded `blockPath.length > 0`, so every top-level attribute of a flat `.hcl`/`.tfvars` document is dropped. Measured pre-fix: 126 corpus files with real content produced ZERO symbols (consul `full-config.hcl` with 30+ top-level attributes, boundary `enos.vars.hcl`, every `*.tfvars` in terraform@db4eef4). Reverted generically: property symbols whose owner is the document root are removed. hcl/flat-attribute-document pins all seven.
#881 regression: removes the execution-boundary guard — quote/discarded/commented forms fabricate calls and phantom definitions (pre-fix behavior)

#881 regression: a leading `#_discard` is treated as the list head, so `(#_ignored quote (trivia-ghost))` is walked as live code instead of a quote form and fabricates calls[caller->trivia-ghost] — the exact shape formNameOf's executionHead rule prevents

#881 head-position regression: metadata is treated as occupying head position, so `(^:probe meta-called)` stops being an ordinary call and meta-head loses calls->meta-called (the widening executionHead introduces at the fixture head-position-881)
#881 regression: syntax-quote prunes live unquote execution — templates loses calls to live-unquote (verified HEAD counterexample)
#881 regression: shadowed comment macro treated as core form — parameter-shadow loses calls to live-argument (verified HEAD counterexample)

W23 regression: re-imposes the constant-group parity skip on `case` defaults — calls inside a LIST-shaped default vanish (`(case k :a 1 (helper-default k))` loses calls->helper-default for both h and j); the case-constants fixture pins them (mirrored fix: analyzer + oracle)

M59 (#825) regression: every edge loses its line_number (the measured pre-fix state: 0/8381 corpus clojure edges lined) — callsite-lines-825's null-line forbid pins the unlined collapse that no expect entry can express absent
M59 (#825): the line is emitted 0-based (every site off by one; line 1 becomes the stored 0 the M59 healing pass exists for) — per-site line pins catch it
ER-D2 parity: call edges lose meta.callArity — `pick/0` and `pick/1` sites become indistinguishable in the payload (the multi-arity merge defect class)
the per-site collapse: edges deduped without the line component, so one callee call site survives per (source,target) — callsite-lines-825 loses its line-9/10 rows
C4 regression: strips comments AND docstring from all symbols (the doc channel is differential-invisible — only the fixture can catch it) — docstrings expectComments pins catch it
C5 regression: aliased protocol targets revert to the raw alias (`p/Proto`) — implements-alias expect AND forbid both fail
C11 regression: the rest marker leaks into parameters (`[& args]` → ["&","args"]) — params forbidParameters names [&] catches it
C10 regression: body vectors leak back into parameters (`(defn leaky [x] [y z])` → [x, y, z]) — params forbidParameters names [y, z] catches it
C9 regression: a reify/extend method impl fabricates a call edge (the measured `use-reify -[calls]-> px` class — here `build -[calls]-> ex`) — extend-reify's calls→ex forbid catches it
C9 regression: protocol-extending forms emit no implements edges (reify/extend-protocol silently absent) — extend-reify expects catch it
C13 regression: a tagged-literal payload is walked as code (`#my/tag (call-x)` emits calls→call-x) — tagged-ctors forbid catches it
C12 regression: a lowercase tagged literal is misread as a constructor (`#my/tag [1 2]` → instantiates my/tag) — tagged-ctors forbid catches it

C7 regression: the top-level require is ignored — its import/references vanish AND the aliased call target reverts to the raw `s/join` (the measured pre-fix state) — toplevel-forms expect+forbid catch both halves
C8 regression: calls outside functions are dropped again (def/defonce initializers, deftest bodies) — toplevel-calls expects catch it

C6 regression: the file complexity fallback reverts to the fabricated `symbols.length` (vars/protocols/modules counted as complexity) — callsite-lines-825's expectMetadata pin catches it (differential-invisible)

C14 regression: the C7/C8 libspec guard is dropped — `(java.util Date)` inside `(:import …)` is walked as a call and fabricates `ns -[calls]-> java.util` (found by the M12 differential as a false positive during CLJ1; import-list forbid catches it)

F5-cert (junit.clj): a keyword-headed data form (`(:ns (meta var))`) fires the ns branch — phantom module symbol + alias-table reset, so later aliased calls go unresolved — kwd-headed-data pins catch both halves

F5-cert (clj-kondo rewrite-clj): a plain-object guard answers `["toString"]` from Object.prototype — every Java-class toString override misfires the method-impl rule, losing the method symbol and consuming its body's calls — tostring-impl pins catch it
F5-cert (clj-kondo node.clj / order.clj): a self-require or self-qualified call emits a self-loop references edge (ELXD8 violation) — self-reference forbid catches it

F5-cert (clj-kondo meta.clj): prefix-list require `[prefix [sub :as a]]` handled as a flat spec — nested sub references dropped and `a/one` left unresolved as `a/one` — prefix-require pins catch both halves
CLJ-ADV F1: the `#(f …)` shorthand head call dropped (body elements walked as argument positions only) — anon-fn-calls pins the lambda->helper edge
CLJ-ADV F2: `(:refer-clojure :exclude [replace reverse])` fed through the libspec handler — the VAR name becomes a fabricated namespace reference (43 corpus files) — refer-clojure forbids catch it

CLJ-ADV F3: the plain-{} namespaceAliases answers `["toString"]` from Object.prototype — the call target becomes the inherited Function source text (the F5-2 class, missed on this record) — proto-alias pins the honest target

CLJ-ADV F4: a DATA-position `comment` symbol (map key) flips the file-global shadow flag — every `(comment …)` body is walked as code (a fabricated call from a scratch block, measured on clj-kondo analyzer.clj)

W23-b regression: shadow ranges collapse back into one file-wide order-blind flag — the data block BEFORE any shadow (w23b-ordered-ghost), the block after the let's region closed (w23b-region-ghost) and a sibling arity clause's data block (w23b-multi-ghost) are all walked as code (the pre-fix fabrication), caught by shadowed-comment-881's three forbidden ghosts

W24-mr1 regression (fixture shadowed-comment-881 shapes C/D/E): letfn fn-spec bindings stop shadowing the comment macro — the spec-head name and spec params emit no ranges again, so `(comment (target))` bodies are dropped as data (three missing live edges; the after-form ghost stays forbidden)

W24-mr2 regression (fixture refer-forms): `:refer` names stop resolving — call targets keep the bare dangling identity (U1-class) and the fixture's qualified expects go missing; locals-wins shapes stay bare either way
W24-mr3 regression (fixture meta-visibility): `^{:private true}` / `^:private` stop counting as private — meta-private vars and fns export as public API again

CLJ-D17 regression (fixture core-gate): the derived clojure.core surface is reverted to a short list — the 286 real core names the hand transcription omitted come back, so `mapcat`/`ex-info`/`transduce`/`dedupe`/`run!`/`with-meta` are emitted as `calls` targets again. This is the defect the F5 differential CANNOT see, because the oracle imports the same list: the fabrication was MIRRORED, which is why it survived three prior waves of this lane

CLJ-D18 regression (fixture core-gate): the in-file shadow exemption is dropped, so a call to a name the FILE defines is suppressed as a standard-library call again — 555 real call sites in the clojure corpus, and the expansion's own safety net: the fixture's `below-the-def` and `region-bound` edges disappear

CLJ-D18 twin (fixture core-gate): the `:refer` exemption is dropped, so a `:refer` of a core-SHAPED name (`[clj.fixture.util :refer [re-find]]`) is suppressed as a standard-library call and the confirmed dependency is lost

CLJ-D19 regression (fixtures proto-members + definterface): the core-builtin gate is put BACK on protocol/interface signature declarations, so members named `alength`, `identity`, `key`, `count` vanish again — gvec.clj's `ArrayManager` shipped with 1 of 5 methods for exactly this reason

R1 (3d4d7fa4) regression: a `qualified` name under a `constant_pattern` stops being read, so a switch case naming a declared enum member publishes no edge again. The pre-fix shape is not a guess — it is what the analyzer did for its whole life, because the string 'qualified' appeared NOWHERE in 2,784 lines of it: `mode == M.off` parses as `identifier(M)` plus `selector(.off)` and the DT-F pass saw the selector, while `case M.off:` parses as ONE `qualified` node and nothing read it. Two node shapes, same text, one handled. Recovery measured at the time: 2,405 edges over ProxiCall/lib, 516 naming a symbol declared in the same file, 0 relationships removed, 0 duplicates introduced. The transform deletes every `uses` edge carrying `isConstantPattern` — exactly the surface the fix added — and leaves the expression-shaped edge alone, so the fixture's CONTRAST pin (`sameTextInExpression -> recipientLookup`, already working before the fix) still passes and the mutant can only be caught by the pattern pins.

R2 (7c574834) regression: the type extractors' node allowlist loses `record_type`, so every Dart 3 record type vanishes from the payload again. All three extractors (parameter, return, field) accepted a fixed five-node list — type_identifier, function_type, nullable_type, void_type — and a record fell through every one: `void f((int, String) p)` typed its parameter `dynamic`, and `({int a, String b}) f()` published no return type at all, so the function looked untyped. DARTD6 and DARTD13 could both be right about their mechanism and still lose every record. The transform rewrites any record-shaped parameter or return type back to `dynamic`, restoring the pre-fix degradation exactly. Measured recovery at the time: 27 return types and 1 parameter over 1,294 ProxiCall/lib files, with 0 relationships changed.

R15 (243dc36f) regression: an arrow function's parameters stop shadowing a same-named file-level symbol, so a read inside the arrow resolves by NAME to the unrelated module declaration. `function f(bbEntry: string) { return (root) => root() }` republishes `references f->root` against a module-level `function root()`. It fell through R12 and R13 for a structural reason: an arrow is not a named declaration, so the reference pass never rebinds its current symbol when it descends into one, and the ENCLOSING function stays current — whose parameter list is a different one (`bbEntry`), so the shadow set was well-formed and simply lacked the name. Measured at the time: 227 false `references` over 1000 tracked files in 66 of them, the largest of the three shadowing defects. The transform re-adds a `references` edge from every symbol to any file-level symbol whose name equals one of the symbol's own parameters, which is the pre-fix arrow shape because the arrow's parameters never reached the shadow set. The fixture's `shadowDoesNotLeak -> file` expectation is the pin that keeps the fix scoped.

PY-11 REVERT: an uppercase callee that is not a class declared in THIS file produces NO relationship at all, instead of a `calls` edge. Measured over 300 pinned corpus files: 1,152 uppercase callees, 263 became `instantiates`, and 889 — 77.2% — produced nothing, of which 368 named a class the file EXPLICITLY IMPORTS. `module = AnsibleModule(...)`, file after file, with nothing in the graph. The transform drops every `calls` edge whose target starts uppercase, which is the pre-fix observable. Caught by python/module-all-exports' class surface and by the call-shape fixtures, and the assertion is the EDGE COUNT because the dropped edges are the ones no fixture happened to name.

PY-4 REVERT: a statement with no enclosing function or class attributes its relationships to the LITERAL STRING "global" — a python KEYWORD used as a scope name. Three things were wrong at once: it is not a name anything can be navigated to (the M60 R7 class, the same one markdown hit when an empty ATX heading published a symbol named `#`); it is absent from the indexer's GENERIC_SOURCE_NAMES (`unknown, SCSS_FILE_SCOPE, window, exports, default, GlobalScope`), the list of names the store knows are synthetic scopes, so python's took a path no other lane's takes; and it contradicted the same analyzer's own `imports` edges in the same file, which already used the module stem. Caught by python/module-all-exports, whose expected `from` is the module name — a lane spelling the scope `global` cannot match it.

PY-13 REVERT: the module scope is the filename stem VERBATIM, so `my-module.py` publishes the scope `my-module` — not a valid python identifier, not typeable, and not a name a symbol could carry. Found by writing the PY-12 fixture: the harness refused to match the expected `from` because the analyzer spelled the module with a hyphen in it. Caught by python/module-all-exports, whose file is `module-all-exports.py` and whose every export edge must be sourced from `module_all_exports` — the unnormalised spelling matches nothing.

PY-14 REVERT: `exports` is read only from a `list` literal, so `__all__ = ("a", "b")` publishes nothing. The tuple spelling is ordinary older python, and measured over 400 pinned corpus files: 16 `__all__` assignments, 13 lists and 3 tuples that produced no edge at all — 19% of a module's declared public surface invisible for a reason that has nothing to do with the author. Caught by python/module-all-exports, whose first `__all__` is a TUPLE, so a lane that reads only lists satisfies every other expectation in the file and misses these three.

PY-7 REVERT, the subtle half: the companion index IS read, the base IS resolved from it, and then the answer is published as if nothing had been learned — every override the index confirmed is demoted from its verified confidence to the 0.5 `first-parent-guess`. The EDGE is still right, so no membership comparison notices: only the number a reader weighs it by changes. Caught by python/companion-index/comp-child, whose `Redirect.send -> Mixin.send` row carries `confidenceMin: 0.9` precisely so a demotion fails it. Why it is worth a mutant when the obvious reverts already exist: dropping the companion read altogether and dropping its RESULT are different defects with different consequences. The first changes the edge SET — and a set comparison catches it immediately. The second leaves the edge set byte-for-byte intact and corrupts only the ranking, which is the failure a graph consumer cannot detect by looking at WHAT is there. 855 corpus edges sit in exactly this state today, and the census that found them had to compare confidences rather than members to see it at all.

PY-24 REVERT: `__all__` is treated as export METADATA only, so an `__all__` assigned in a CLASS body publishes exports and never becomes a class member. `__all__` is in that class's `__dict__` like any other assignment, so this drops a real `contains` edge — the corpus row `contains CythonDotParallel -> __all__` at cython/Cython/Shadow.py, which was the last missing relationship left in the whole python corpus. Caught by python/class-dunder-all-is-not-exports. NOTE ON WHAT THIS MUTANT CANNOT EXPRESS: the revert had a second half — publishing `exports module -> alpha/beta` for names inside a class `__all__` — and that half is NOT reproducible here. It is an ABSENCE of scope information in the result: once the gate is correct, nothing in `r` records which `__all__` literals were skipped, so a result-shaped transform cannot re-add them. Reconstructing them from fixture strings is what the `dunder-all-tuple-ignored` comment above records as having produced a no-op that reported 0 -> 0 and read as a survivor. The false-exports half is therefore covered ONLY by the fixture's three forbid rows, which is the honest split: a mutant that cannot be written without guessing names is a mutant that proves nothing.

PY-15 REVERT: ONE marker root is removed from the detection table while the rest of the table stays exactly as declared, so the surface still reports itself alive and still passes every reachability check — the defect the table's own comment warns about ('a marker that stops matching is a visible deletion here and not a silent loss of detection') made invisible by making it small. This is the shape the coverage census found in the wild rather than a shape invented for the harness: 7 of 9 declared roots fired ZERO times across 3,271 corpus files, and nothing in the suite noticed, because reachability had been reported as coverage. The transform drops the LAST declared root from `frameworkPatterns` and re-picks the primary from what remains, which is the pre-census table minus its newest row. Caught by python/framework-marker-coverage, whose `detectedFrameworks` row is an EXACT ORDERED list, and by python/framework-surface-pins.

REVERT of the first genuine analyzer defect the independent oracle found: a class written in a CLASS BODY loses its owner again, so no `contains` is derived for it. `Outer.Inner` resolves in python with no lookup machinery, so the nesting is containment rather than a lexical coincidence, and the pre-fix state was 66 `contains` edges the tree supports and the lane did not emit, across 24 corpus files including `_Multipart._Part` in `urllib/parse.py`. The transform drops `ownerName`/`ownerKind` from class symbols whose metadata says `isNestedClass`, which is the pre-fix state exactly. Caught by python/nested-class-containment, whose `contains Outer -> Inner` row is the fix and whose FORBID row — `contains Outer -> Local`, a class in a METHOD — is what stops the eager version from passing: the mutant models the lazy side, the forbid models the eager side, and a change that gets the containment without the guard satisfies one and fails the other.

REVERT of the fourth genuine analyzer defect, and the most damaging of the four: a class VARIABLE on a base is made indistinguishable from a METHOD, so the name-keyed match finds it and the lane publishes an override that overrides nothing — at 0.95, with no `reasonCode`, which reads as a verified fact. `class Base: attr = None` beside `class Derived(Base): def attr(self)` published `Derived.attr -> Base.attr`. There is no method on Base to override: `Base.attr` is the value `None`, which CPython's own `ast` reports as `attr(var)` against `attr(def)`.

The transform PROMOTES the variable's SYMBOL KIND rather than clearing a flag, and that distinction is the whole lesson of writing it: a first version cleared `isClassVariable` in metadata and reported `0 -> 0` — a survivor — because the fix reads `kind`, not that flag. A mutant has to move the field the resolution actually consults. Reproducing the pre-fix observable means reproducing the pre-fix *indistinguishability*, not editing the nearest metadata.

Caught by python/class-variable-is-not-overridden, whose three positives are the half that must survive: a fix that stopped matching on name at all would pass every forbid in that fixture and lose real overrides. In the corpus this was 20 fabricated VERIFIED edges in `Cython/Compiler/Nodes.py`, where Cython declares class state at class level so nearly every method shares a name with a variable on its base.

The EAGER side of the binding-scope line: a class-body variable binding is suppressed outright, not only when a lambda or comprehension encloses it. Every Property carrying `isClassVariable` is dropped along with its `contains` edge, so no class body publishes a member at all. This is the direction a fix for the lambda-parameter fabrication is most likely to overshoot into — 'stop publishing names bound in a scope' is one step from 'stop publishing names bound in a class body' — and the two differ on every real member: `walrus_direct` IS a class attribute in python, verified with `vars()`, as are `via_lambda` and `from_comprehension`. Caught by python/lambda-scope-is-not-class-scope, whose positives were read out of CPython rather than asserted, which is the only reason this line has both directions pinned: the fabrication side by FORBID rows and the over-suppression side by positive rows. A fixture carrying only one of the two would accept half the possible fixes. Stated honestly: the faithful revert of the scope guard itself cannot be written here, because the guard asks a question about the TREE and a ParseResult does not carry one. A no-op reporting 0 -> 0 would have looked like a survivor while modelling nothing, which is the trap three earlier mutants in this lane fell into.

The class-member OWNER is dropped from every symbol. Nothing in the analyzer fails when this happens — the result still parses, still extracts every symbol, and still emits every `overrides` edge with its correct `Owner.method` source string. The damage is one layer down, in the store: `parallel-indexer.ts` builds `nameToSymbol` with TWO keys per symbol, `name` and `${s.scope || s.ownerName}.${name}`, and the owner-qualified key is the one that makes an `overrides` source resolve to the RIGHT method when several classes in a file declare the same name. Strip `ownerName` and every one of those edges falls back to a bare leaf lookup, which is first-wins. This is the surviving half of the retracted PY-3: the dependency is real and it is load-bearing, so the pin has to be checked rather than assumed. Caught by the `contains` derivation, which reads the same field — which is the honest reason this mutant is caught at all, and worth stating plainly rather than discovering later that the override path itself is unpinned.

R8 (M60) regression: the emitted array follows IMPORT order instead of the marker table, so a file that imports pytest before django reports pytest as its primary framework. The contract puts application frameworks first and test frameworks last (csharp's CS_FRAMEWORK_ORDER rule, CONV-CS-2), because import order is a property of how a file is sorted rather than of the code. Caught by python/framework-surface-pins, which imports pytest FIRST and pins [Django, Flask, pytest] plus a Django primary pick.

#902 regression: `callLeafName` goes back to the `namedChild(0)` fallthrough for any callee shape it does not list, so a parenthesised CONDITIONAL callee names its `if` branch (`calls conditional -> f`), a parameterless LAMBDA names its body (`calls lam -> f`), and a parameterised LAMBDA names its PARAMETER (`calls lam_param -> y`) — calls the source never writes, all refused by the differential's oracle, and all three MEASURED on the full cython draw (475 files: withstat_py.py:218, extra_walrus.py:136 naming `y_global`, extra_walrus.py:151 naming `z`, seq_mul.py:159 naming `n`). The injected set is exactly what the fallback produced on the fixture: a conditional_expression's first named child is its consequence, a lambda's is its `parameters` node whose first named child is the parameter, and a parameterless lambda's is its body. Caught by python/callee-shapes' three forbid pins.

#902's sibling in the BASE position: `baseClassLeaf` goes back to the `namedChild(0)` fallthrough, so a base written as a CALL names the FACTORY FUNCTION as the parent class (`extends Computed -> factory`) — measured on cython:python as `extends T -> namedtuple` at Tools/dataclass_test_data/test_dataclasses.py:1637, the one UNEXPLAINED edge the #902 fix exposed. The same fallback also restores PYD6's keyword fabrication (`extends Keyword -> total`, the pre-fix blanket descent over a `total=False` argument). Caught by python/base-shapes' two forbid pins.

#748 regression: a shadowed earlier `def` is published again as if it were live — a SECOND symbol for the same (container, name), its body's call graph, its member reads and declared-type references, and its cyclomatic decision points. That is the pre-fix reading, and the reason the corpus could not convict it: MEASURED 0 duplicate-name scopes across cython 475 + requests 37 files, so no differential sample ever draws one. The injected set is exactly what the keep-both analyzer produced on this fixture (module-level `top` twice at 44/49, class-body `C.foo` twice at 54/58, `calls top -> phantom_marker` at 45, `uses foo -> dead_read` at 55, `references foo -> DeadType` at 56, complexity 3 = base 1 + the live `if alt_flag` + the phantom's `if phantom_marker`). Caught by python/dupdef-last-wins on all four halves at once.

#748's OTHER failure mode: the rule is applied to every same-name group instead of only to a genuine rebinding, so a DECLARATION CHAIN loses its members — the `@overload` stubs (one symbol where there are three, and the surviving one is the implementation rather than the first stub) and the `@property` getter (the chain keeps 2, the blanket rule keeps 1) go away, and the getter's member read goes with them. That is not hypothetical: MEASURED range-keyed over the pinned corpora, 21 of the 25 duplicate-name scopes are chains (5 @overload groups in cython's Shadow.py, 9 in requests, 7 property-accessor chains), so the blanket reading deletes real symbols and real setter bodies corpus-wide. Caught by python/dupdef-last-wins' chain pins (count 3 and 2, the first stub's startLine, and the getter's `uses size -> _size`).

R8 (M60) regression: the emitted array goes back to the OBSERVATION-map order, which is the pre-fix observable — the analyzer iterated `frameworksObj` and pushed as it went, so the payload was whichever order the walk visited triggers in. Caught by swift/framework-surface-pins, which imports Foundation and UIKit FIRST and pins [SwiftUI, Combine, UIKit, Foundation] with SwiftUI as the primary pick: the mutant emits [Foundation, UIKit, SwiftUI, Combine] and picks Foundation, so the array pin, the primary pin and the patterns pin all fail.

R8 (M60) regression: the lane detects frameworks and publishes no PRIMARY PICK, which is exactly what swift did before this round — measured at 0 of 81 detecting files on the deterministic draw. Every consumer that keys on the primary framework then reads an iOS file as framework-less while `detectedFrameworks` says otherwise. Caught by swift/framework-surface-pins' expectPrimaryFramework and by the R8 runtime probe's A3 assertion.

R8 (M60) regression: the lane publishes the detection array without `frameworkPatterns` — the other half of the contract the lane never emitted before this round. The two keys are not redundant: detection says WHICH framework, the patterns say what was observed and therefore why. Caught by swift/framework-surface-pins' frameworkPatterns metadata pin, which pins the whole array and its order.

R8 (M60) regression: the emitted array goes back to the SET'S INSERTION ORDER, which is the pre-fix observable — the analyzer published `[...frameworks]` and picked `[...frameworks][0]`, so the payload was the order the `#import` statements happened to be walked in. Caught by objc/framework-surface-pins, which imports Foundation and Cocoa FIRST and pins [UIKit, AppKit, Cocoa, Foundation] with UIKit as the primary pick: the mutant emits [Foundation, Cocoa, AppKit, UIKit] and picks Foundation — the base library every Objective-C file imports, reported as the primary framework of a UIKit view.

R8 (M60) regression: the lane goes back to publishing `detectedFrameworks` and a primary pick and NOTHING ELSE — the state the census registered as missing-contract-key and the runtime half measured on 7 of 7 detecting files over 153 real corpus files. `frameworkPatterns` is not a redundant copy of detection: it says what was observed and therefore why the framework is claimed. Caught by objc/framework-surface-pins' frameworkPatterns metadata pin, and by the R8 runtime probe's A7 assertion — which exists because this exact shape measured CLEAN before it was added.

ER-D36 regression: counts a BARE unquoted atom in type syntax as a type dependency again. In Erlang `-type day() :: monday | tuesday.` declares the ATOMS monday and tuesday — you must write `monday()` to apply a type — so every such edge is fabricated, resolving to a same-named type or record property elsewhere in the file. This is the M12 false positive that started the ER3 wave: the differential went 1.000 -> 0.784 with 19 of them, two of them this exact shape (`job -> id`, `job -> kind`, the map keys of a map type). types-er3 FORBIDS `handle -> ok`, `handle -> error` and `payload -> undefined` while still REQUIRING the applied `binary()`, `request()` and `reply()`, so the mutant has to be selective to survive

M59.A7 (#825) regression: csharp's relationships go back to carrying NO line — the exact pre-fix state (MEASURED: 23,924 relationships, 0 withLine, on a 200-file draw of the pinned corpus, the M59 oracle reading 0/23,924). Caught by csharp/callsite-lines-825, which pins every edge type's line.

M59.A7 (#825) regression: every lined edge goes back one line — the CONSTRUCT's start instead of the node that names the target (a callee's receiver, `new` before the constructed type, the `:` before a wrapped `base()`, the attribute or return type before a wrapped name). Exactly the positions csharp/callsite-lines-825 forbids.

M59.A7 (#825) regression, the class this round MEASURED on the corpus: a `contains` edge claims the target SYMBOL's range start, which for an attributed or wrapped declaration is a line the member's name is not written on (653 of 23,924 relationships — 100% of the round's inconsistent set). Simulated off the result's own symbol table (owner+name), so it stays faithful rather than name-hardcoded.

M59.A7 (#825) regression: the SYNTHESISED member names go back to claiming a line. `constructor` and `Finalize` are written nowhere in the source (a constructor is written `ClassName(...)`, a destructor `~ClassName()`), so the only honest state is no line — MEASURED: 366 such claims on a 200-file draw, which the M59 oracle can classify only as uncheckable. Caught by csharp/callsite-lines-825's `line_number: null` pins and its forbid entries for the declaration lines.

M60.R7 (csharp lane) regression: a `params T[] name` parameter is dropped again — the exact pre-fix state, because the grammar does not wrap the params form in a `parameter` node and the old loop read named `parameter` children only. Simulated by removing array-typed parameters, which is WIDER than the defect by construction: the published output cannot tell a `params` parameter from an ordinary array parameter (the node type is gone), so the mutant also hits `int[] data` — which is why the fixture pins that control, and why the fixture is the only place that fails both ways.

M60.R7 (csharp lane) regression: an unresolvable parameter type publishes the literal `"unknown"` again — the register's csharp entry (`pType = … || "unknown"`). Caught by csharp/param-type-honesty's forbidParameters types.

M60.R7 (csharp lane) regression: `extractTypeString`'s last-resort scan lands on the parameter's OWN NAME again and the name is published as the type (`void M(int a, b)` -> type `"b"`, MEASURED). Caught by csharp/param-type-honesty's forbidParameters types for both positions.

M60.R7 (csharp lane) regression: the empty-name guard around the params branch is removed, so the grammar's recovery identifier (which the tree writes EMPTY — measured with script/m14/tmp/cs-param-noname-tree.ts) is published as a parameter with a blank name. Scoped by symbol name because the shape has no output-level signature of its own: an empty list is indistinguishable from a symbol whose list never existed, so NamelessParams is the only observable anchor. Caught by csharp/param-type-honesty's forbidParameters names entry for the blank name.

M60.R1 regression: the using-alias form publishes the ALIAS as the imported module again (`using Alias = Plain;` -> module/target `Alias`, with the real target named nowhere) — the pre-R1 behavior, measured with script/m14/tmp/cs-using-alias-probe.ts. Caught by csharp/using-alias-and-operators' forbidRelationships on both alias spellings.

M60.R1 regression: conversion operators go back to the DEAD-BRANCH name `operator <target>` (the old pattern expected `operator implicit …`, the wrong token order, so it never matched real C# and the implicit/explicit twins — two distinct members — collided). Simulated off the result's own symbols: an operator whose name starts with `implicit `/`explicit ` is rewritten to `operator <target>`. Caught by csharp/using-alias-and-operators (expects both twins AND forbids the collapsed name) and by csharp/payload-and-complexity's corrected `implicit int` pin.

M60.R1 regression: a conversion target goes back to being TRUNCATED at the first space — the old regex class `[^\s(]+` stopped there, so `implicit operator Box < Plain > (…)` published `implicit Box`. Caught by csharp/using-alias-and-operators' expectSymbols (`implicit Box<Plain>`) and its forbidSymbols entry for the truncated spelling.

M60.R1 regression: the `checked` operator goes back to colliding with its unchecked twin (`operator checked +` -> `operator +`) — the shape the old regex handled only by luck, through a text capture of a token that is a grammar FIELD now. Caught by csharp/using-alias-and-operators, which pins both spellings on one type.

D1 revert: the leaf-only walk of a QUALIFIED name comes back, so a qualified generic's type arguments are never walked and the declared-type graph publishes only the base — the dependency this graph's own header calls "the real dependency", lost because the source wrote the path out. tree-sitter-c-sharp spells `System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, Widget>` as `qualified_name [ …, generic_name [ identifier, type_argument_list ] ]`, so the leaf descent reaches the identifier and never the argument list. Simulated from the SOURCE (the result no longer records which declaration was written qualified): every argument of a qualified generic base on the same line as a base edge is dropped. Caught by csharp/generic-name-positions' expectRelationships for QualifiedHolder.Map / Pair / Nested / Tupled and the parameter, return and property positions — the PLAIN twin PlainHolder.Map keeps its argument, so the pair is the pin.

D2 revert, both halves at once because they are one cause: the attribute-name predicate goes back to naming three node types (so a GENERIC attribute's `generic_name` name child matches none and the decorator is DROPPED), and the payload goes back to the raw node text (so the qualified twin that still matches publishes the WHOLE generic spelling, `System.Marker<int>`). Simulated from the result: every decorator carrying a type argument is truncated to the raw spelling, and one decorator per symbol is deleted to reproduce the dropped half. Caught by csharp/generic-name-positions' expectDecorators (the generic shapes must be present at all) AND its forbidDecorators entries for `<` — the negative half is what makes it catchable, because `System.Marker<int>` CONTAINS `System.Marker` and an expect alone can never fail on this revert (CSD16's exact finding).

D3 revert: a using ALIAS whose target is a type expression publishes the EXPRESSION as the module and the `references` target again — `Dictionary<string,Widget>`, and with a tuple argument the element NAMES too — and the separate argument edges go away. Simulated off the result: every import module carrying a type argument is restored to the full spelling, and the `using_type_argument` edges are dropped. Caught by csharp/generic-name-positions' forbidRelationships on the three expression spellings and its expectRelationships for the argument edges — the arguments are the half that a strip-only fix would silently lose, so they are pinned positively, not just negatively.

D3's second half, and the one a reviewer would call cosmetic until it is read: the `using_type_argument` edge copies the module edge's `isUsingDirective`/`isImport` flags, so classifyEvidenceTier stamps a TYPE reference with the import evidence class. THIS MUTANT SURVIVED ITS FIRST RUN — the fixture pinned `meta.relationshipType` on the argument edges and a test written only on TARGETS cannot see an evidence class at all, so the claim it names was unpinnable. Rather than delete the claim, the fixture now pins `meta.evidenceClass` on all four using rows (the module's `import_based` and the argument's `reference_qualified`), which is the contract `classifyEvidenceTier` actually keys on. Caught by csharp/generic-name-positions' expectRelationships `meta.evidenceClass` rows.

CS-D6 revert: the field-access `uses` pass drops a member READ whenever the enclosing function already has a `calls` edge to the same member NAME — the pre-fix guard `!emittedCalls.has(`${src}->${tgt}`)`, keyed with no site. It duplicates `isCallee`, which already decides this structurally by span, and in C# a static member and a call can share a name, so real reads vanish. Simulated off the RESULT, the way the pre-fix output is derived: for every function that has both a `uses` and a `calls` edge to the same target, the `uses` row is removed. Caught by csharp/read-collides-with-call's expectRelationships for ReadAndCallSameName.Count, ReadAndCallMember.Report, ReadAndCallNegate.Negate and CallOnly.Negate.

CS-D8 revert: a parameter's declared TYPE, and a type ARGUMENT in a local declaration's type, are published as `uses` reads. Pre-fix this emitted `uses TakesGadget -> Gadget` at confidence 1.0, stamped on the SIGNATURE line with the enclosing method as its source, so a type read as a read inside the method body. 6 rows over 200 roslyn files; the corpus shapes are `SemanticModel semanticModel` where the class also has a `SemanticModel` member, and `Func<Gadget, Gadget>` where the name is a type argument nested inside a generic_name two levels below the declaration that owns the type. The shadowing frames cannot help: the shadow and the read would be the same identifier.

CS-D7 revert: a declared TYPE is published as a `uses` read of the member that declares it, in two positions. A FIELD's type is not a direct child of `field_declaration` (the grammar nests it under `variable_declaration`), so the old `isCSharpEntityName` first-direct-identifier rule never saw it; and for a PROPERTY the first direct identifier is the TYPE, so the rule took the type and let the property's own NAME through. Both fabrications resolve precisely because the type name collides with a member of the same class, and the shadowing frame cannot help — the shadow and the read are the same identifier. Simulated from the SHAPE the pre-fix analyzer published, which is why it reads off the declared-type edges rather than off existing `uses` rows: a `declared_type` reference whose target is ALSO a member name of the same owner is exactly the collision that made the pre-fix bare-identifier pass resolve, and the pre-fix pass stamped it with the DECLARATION's line. Caught by csharp/read-collides-with-call's forbidRelationships for `Collides -> Widget` (the field) and `Widget -> Widget` (the property's own name) — both already covered as `references` by the declared-type graph, which is why losing them costs no coverage.

The `.dcl` ruling reverted: a module-level `type_signature` publishes nothing, so a definition module's declared interface is invisible (measured: 2,002 distinct module-level signature names over the lane's 312 files, 708 published nowhere). Caught by clean/definition-module-interface — its expectSymbols entries for interfaceFunction/NSMakeSize/%./bitxor and their expectExports twins.

The merge resolved the WRONG way: the declaration's range wins instead of the definition's, so a merged symbol points at its prototype line. Caught by clean/signature-definition-merge's expectSymbolRanges (mergeTarget startLine 20 = the definition line; the declaration is 19).

The merge broken the other way: the declaration is kept BESIDE the definition instead of being replaced by it, so one name is published as two symbols. Caught by clean/signature-definition-merge's expectSymbolCount (`mergeTarget` equals 1) — measured catch, printed by script/m14/tmp/mutant-catch-reasons.ts; the same regression inside the analyzer's own export loop would additionally trip the exports-family invariant, which is why the fixture pins both halves.

Pre-fix state: an `operator_definition` — a different node from `function_declaration`, and the Clean norm for Eq/Ord instance members — is not a callable, so its body's applications are attributed to nobody (measured: 39 real module-level + 192 instance-member operator definitions). Caught by clean/signature-definition-merge's `calls ++. -> helper`.

Pre-fix state: an operator is never released when its scope exits, so it swallows the next module-level application — the exact defect the exhaustive mini-differential found as `calls ++| -> flatten` in clean-stdlib/StdOverloadedList.icl (the operator claiming a call from a macro six lines below it). Caught by clean/signature-definition-merge's forbidRelationships entry for `calls ++. -> tweak`.

Pre-fix export predicate: `!sym.ownerName`, the exact negation of the rule the block's own comment stated, so a file exported nothing but its own module symbol (measured: 312 of 312 corpus files exported at most one thing — 295 exports against 6,031 module-owned symbols). Caught by every clean fixture's expectExports.

The name-keyed export dedupe removed: a file that publishes one name in two KINDS offers it twice. Reached honestly — `instance == Collision` publishes its Class under the instance TARGET type, so 59 of the lane's 312 corpus files collided. Caught by clean/instance-target-name-collision via the exports-family invariant.

The pre-dimension-8 state: every relationship is published with no `line_number` field at all (measured: 0 of 11,108 edges named a site before this landed; the store can then navigate an edge to nothing). Caught by every line_number constraint in the lane's fixtures — expression-shapes (5 pins), signature-definition-merge (4), instance-target-name-collision (4), definition-module-interface (4), import-modules-alias-884 (4) — and by F9-PROBE-CLEAN-EDGE-LINE's coverage clause.

The line stays but the dedupe key goes back to `source|type|target`, i.e. PER-SET: the first site's line is kept and every later site's edge is swallowed (measured on the corpus: 1,722 edges belong to multi-site groups, so this collapses them). Caught by the per-site half of the pins — expression-shapes' `contains ExpressionShapes -> Point` at BOTH 19 and 31 with expectRelationshipCount equals 2, likewise instance-target-name-collision's two `contains -> Collision` lines, and F9-PROBE-CLEAN-EDGE-LINE's `calls f` at three distinct lines. A fixture pinning only `line_number: <one line>` would NOT catch this — which is why those pins are written in pairs.

`type C = ref object` goes back to a bare `type`. The pre-fix rule read the `object` keyword and missed the `ref_type` wrapper, so every identity-bearing class in the language — the shape inheritance and dynamic dispatch exist for — was published as a type-level name. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Shape, class} and {Rect, class}.

The mirror of the mutant above, and the one that keeps the first honest: over-applying `ref` would turn a copying `object` into a class. `Builder` and `Registry` are plain `object`s. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Builder, struct} and {Registry, struct}.

`type Addable = concept` goes back to a `type`. A concept is the language's structural interface — satisfied by implicit dispatch, no nominal subtype anywhere — which is exactly what SymbolKind.Interface means in this codebase. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Addable, interface}.
`type Color = enum` goes back to a `type`, losing the enum kind. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Color, enum}.

Enum members stop being symbols. `Red`, `Green` and `Blue` are the values code actually compares on, and a variant object's `of Red:` discriminates on them. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Red/Green/Blue, enum_member}.

Object fields stop being symbols, so every property access in the language has no declaration to resolve to. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {name, property}, {w, property} and the rest of the eight.

`iterator countUp` goes back to a macro. An iterator is callable and is reached by `for … in countUp(3)`, so classifying it as a macro breaks the one symbol kind that has a call syntax of its own. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {countUp, function}.

`template twice` goes back to a function. A template is hygienic and is expanded before name resolution, so it is not a callable value; the macro kind is what keeps it out of the call graph as a runtime edge. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {twice, macro}.

`method describe` goes back to a function, which costs the receiver: the override edge is owner-qualified (`Rect.describe -> Shape.describe`) and a method is the only kind that carries one. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {describe, method} and by the overrides pin that names `Rect.describe`.

A file-scope `let` goes back to a `constant`. Nim's `let` is a single immutable binding and `const` is compile-time; collapsing them loses the distinction that tells a reader whether a value exists at runtime. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Greeting, variable}.
A file-scope `const` goes back to a `variable` — the same collapse from the other side, so the pair cannot both pass by being quiet. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {MaxItems, constant}.

`type Pair = tuple[x, y: int]` goes back to a `type`. A tuple type has fields exactly as an object does, and the field names are destructurable (`let (a, b) = pair`), so the struct kind is what lets `x`/`y` be properties. Caught by nim/contract's expectSymbols {Pair, struct}.

`type Registry*[T] = object` publishes `T` as a type symbol. A generic parameter is bound by the declaration, not declared by it, so `T` is not something the index can resolve a reference to. Caught by nim/contract's forbidSymbols {T, type}.

Import edges stop being emitted at all, which empties the module dependency graph — the one relationship an LSP "what does this file depend on" query cannot answer without. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {imports, (global) -> std/os} and the five sibling import pins.

Import edges come back as `references`. This is the defect the differential could not see: the oracle and the analyzer agreed, both were 0-unexplained, and every NIM dependency edge was still invisible to the reader that looks at relationship_type IN ('imports','exports'). Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {type: imports, (global) -> ./mac}.

A relative import publishes no edge. The pre-fix rule only read the infix path shape, and the leading `./` is a PREFIX operator, so every `import ./sibling` in a module vanished — measured 0 imports for a three-file module whose files all import each other relatively, while the same analyzer returned imports for `import std/os`. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {imports, -> ./helpers} and {imports, -> ../shared}.

A path deeper than two segments publishes no edge. The grammar models the separator as a NAMED `operator` node whose text is the whole token (`/`, or `/../` fused with a parent hop), so `op.type` is never `/` and the pre-fix identifier/identifier test never matched: 171 deep-path imports across 141 corpus files and 434 multi-segment relative imports across 299 files published nothing, and because the whole path vanished there was no dangling target to surface it. Caught by nim/contract's expectImports {module: std/private/specialpaths} and its expectRelationships sibling.

`import std/[os, strutils]` publishes ONE edge for the whole list instead of one per element, so a two-module import becomes a single dependency on a name no file has. Caught by nim/contract's expectImports {module: std/os} AND {module: std/strutils} — one pin alone would pass, which is why both are there.

`from ./nativesettings import …` publishes the target `nativesettings` while `import ./configure` publishes `./configure`: two spellings for one module in one graph, from two path readers inside one analyzer. Found by the differential on prologue's application.nim, three edges disagreeing in both directions. Caught by nim/contract's expectImports {module: ./macros, meta.nimFromImport} and its expectRelationships sibling.

Ownership edges stop being emitted, so no symbol has a parent and every method and field is an orphan in the graph. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {contains, Shape -> name} and {contains, Color -> Red}.

Call edges stop being emitted. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {calls, exercise -> makeRect} and {calls, build -> join} — the second is a UFCS call, so the pair also pins that `b.parts.join(",")` has no dot-call node and the member leaf is the callee.

Value-read edges stop being emitted. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {uses, exercise -> Greeting} and {uses, build -> parts} — the second is the member leaf of a UFCS read, which is a `uses` edge distinct from the `calls` edge on the same expression.
Declared-type edges stop being emitted, so a signature no longer states what it accepts. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {references, area -> Rect} and {references, exercise -> Builder}.
Object construction stops being an `instantiates` edge. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {instantiates, makeRect -> Rect}.
Inheritance edges stop being emitted. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {extends, Rect -> Shape}.
Override edges stop being emitted, so a derived method reads as a new method rather than a replacement. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {overrides, Rect.describe -> Shape.describe}.

An override target goes back to the BARE method name, so `Rect.describe` and `Shape.describe` become the same target and the edge says a method overrides itself. Receiver qualification is the only thing that distinguishes an override from a same-named sibling. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {overrides, from: Rect.describe} — the pin is on the SOURCE spelling for exactly this reason.

`Rect(name: "r", …)` publishes `uses makeRect -> name`, i.e. a read of the field `name` that never happens. Nim has no ternary, so `x: value` in an expression only ever names a field of a construction or a variant branch — it never reads one. The edge resolves to a real symbol, so no dangling check could ever catch it. Caught by nim/contract's forbidRelationships {uses, target: name}.

A destructuring binding never enters its scope frame, so a later read of that name is attributed to a same-named field elsewhere in the file. `let (_, name, _) = splitFile(f)` is a tuple_deconstruct_declaration WRAPPING its bindings, and the pre-fix binder took only children typed symbol_declaration, so the whole node was skipped. Measured on pixie: `name` was unbound, and the read at `images.add((name, image))` was published as `uses renderEmojiSet -> name`, pointing at a struct property declared 26 lines earlier and unrelated to the binding. Caught by nim/contract's forbidRelationships {uses, from: stemOf, target: fileStem}, which is only a real assertion because the paired expectSymbols {fileStem, property} pins that the field exists — otherwise a fix that deleted the field would satisfy the forbid vacuously.

A call's callee is published as a `uses` read as well as a `calls` edge, so one call site produces two edges to one target. The pre-fix rule ran the bare-identifier read pass without excluding the callee subtree. Caught by nim/contract's forbidRelationships {uses, target: makeRect} — the callee is in the symbols, so the read pass could have claimed it.

The left side of an assignment is published as a value read. `written = b.parts.len` would then carry a `uses build -> written` edge where the language has one write and one read of something else. Caught by nim/contract's forbidRelationships {uses, from: build, target: written} — the pin has to be on the SOURCE because a target-only pin would also forbid the legitimate reads of `written` elsewhere in the file.

`echo`, `discard` and the numeric conversions become call targets. These are compiler builtins and keywords, and an edge to them is a dependency on a name no file declares — the shape the house precedent suppresses for java's println and groovy's printf. Caught by nim/contract's forbidRelationships {calls, target: echo}, {calls, target: discard} and {calls, target: float}.
`_` — the blank identifier, which appears in every destructuring pattern and every `proc f(_: int)` signature — is published as a variable. Caught by nim/contract's forbidSymbols {_, variable}.

Relationships stop carrying a line at all. A relationship with no line cannot be shown in a file, and the seam gate's out-of-range check has nothing to check. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships line_number pins on an import, a contains, an overrides and a uses edge — four different name sites, because a rule that anchored every edge to one node's line would satisfy a single pin.

An import's line becomes the line of the `import` KEYWORD rather than of the module token. A multi-line `import` puts the paths on later lines than the keyword, so this points a reader at the wrong line for every such edge — and the corpus's own `nim/compiler/nimsets.nim` is the example: `import` on line 12, `ast, astalgo, …` on line 13. Caught by nim/contract's expectRelationships {imports, -> ../shared, line_number} on a `from` import whose keyword and operand are on the same line but whose OPERAND is the evidence.

Every edge is stamped `evidenceClass: "structural"`, erasing the distinction the taxonomy depends on: ownership and inheritance are structural facts, while a read, a call and a construction are contextual, a type name reached through a qualifier is reference_qualified, and a type resolved through an import graph is import_based. A flat tier makes a guess look like a fact. Caught by nim/contract's four meta.evidenceClass pins, including two DIFFERENT tiers on the SAME kind (references: area->Rect reference_qualified, makeRect->Rect import_based).

Every symbol's cyclomatic complexity becomes 1 — the shape a complexity counter lands in when its decision-point node types do not match the grammar, which is a real failure mode found in other lanes (perl's counter was 1 for almost every file because six node-type literals were dead). Caught by nim/contract's expectComplexity {exercise, equals 3} and {countUp, equals 2}.

Documentation comments stop reaching the symbol. Nim's `##` doc comment is how a proc documents its contract, and losing it is invisible in a symbol count. Caught by nim/contract's expectDocstrings on `area`, whose `## Area of a rectangle.` is the fixture's only doc comment.

Pragmas stop being published as decorators. `{.inline.}` is a calling-convention contract and `{.base.}` is the method-dispatch marker that tells a reader which `describe` is the root of the override chain — losing it makes the override edge unexplainable from the symbol alone. Caught by nim/contract's expectDecorators pinning `inline` on `area` and `base` on `describe`.

A macro imported from another file stops publishing its import, leaving `discard retTrue()` calling a name the file never declares — a dangling edge, and the reason nim/contract forbids `retTrue` as a SYMBOL in the first place. The call edge itself is legitimate (the macro really is called); the mutant removes the edge that explains where it came from. Caught by nim/contract's expectImports {module: ./mac, meta.nimFromImport} together with its forbidSymbols {retTrue, function} — the pair, because either alone would pass.

PRE-FIX: `interface_method_declaration`, `interface_property_declaration` and `interface_event_declaration` were in NEITHER DECLARATION_NODES nor SILENT_INTERNAL, which is the whole defect -- nothing visited them, so every interface was published as an EMPTY SHELL with a name and no members, while the class implementing it had all of them. Found by the F8 node-type census, which counted 146 distinct named node types in the corpus against 42 classified: the `every construct is accounted for` claim was 29% true and nothing had measured it. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping interface-owned members. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `IMeasurable` to own `Area` and `Label`.

PRE-FIX: NO OPERATOR WAS EVER PUBLISHED, for two independent reasons. `operator_declaration` has no `name` field -- the operator is an anonymous token -- so the same empty-name guard that hid constructors hid every operator; and `visitOperator` then skipped that very token because `isKeyword` returns true for any token not starting with a letter, which was meant to reject `(` but also rejected every operator SYMBOL. Word operators (`Operator CType`) fail a second time: the keyword and the word are inlined away and exist nowhere in the tree, so there is no node to name from. Found by the F8 census, which found `operator_declaration` classified as a declaration while the walker never produced one. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping symbols named by the operator contract literal. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects an `operator` symbol owned by `Square` and its containment edge.

PRE-FIX: `modifierNames` read `childForFieldName("modifiers")`, which returns ONE node — and this grammar emits the field REPEATEDLY, once per modifier. `Public Overrides Sub` is `modifiers: (...) modifiers: (...)`, so the read returned `public` and dropped `overrides` silently. Every modifier-dependent fact was wrong wherever the modifier was not written first: `Public Shared Sub` reported isStatic=false, `Public Overrides` published ZERO overrides edges across 435 files, and `Const` fields were published as Variables, with `MustOverride`, `ReadOnly` and `NotInheritable` missed the same way. VB writes `Public` first by convention, so the one modifier that was ever read was the one least worth reading. Found because the documentation claimed `overrides` was published and it was not. Simulated as a faithful revert: drop the modifiers that are not the first, which is exactly what the singular read did. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, whose `MaxDepth` is a `constant` and not a `variable`, and whose `Size`/`Reset` carry `Overridable`.

PRE-FIX: `Private _watcher As New Timers.Timer()` puts an `array_type` in `declared_type` -- the `()` reads as bounds -- and the naming helper had no case for that wrapper, so the field published `references _watcher -> "Timers.Timer()"`: the whole expression, parens included. Not a name in the file, not navigable, and unmatchable by any independent oracle. Found by auditing `references`, the label that had been 37% of the index and agreed with by no second implementation. Reverted from the SOURCE rather than a hardcoded string, because the pre-fix target is the grammar node's own text and the fixed result no longer carries it; reading the `As New T(...)` the fixture actually contains is also what keeps this from silently ceasing to match when the fixture changes.

PRE-FIX SHAPE, not a pre-fix absence: the `overrides` edge named the base member by its bare name, so `Public Overrides Property Size` published `overrides Size -> Size` — a SELF-EDGE. A self-edge is not navigable and cannot answer the only question anyone asks of it, "what does this override?"; the same un-navigable shape the member-level `implements` edge had before it was qualified to `IThing.Refresh`. Simulated by stripping the base-type qualifier from the target, which is the pre-fix string exactly. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `overrides Size -> Square.Size` and forbids `overrides Size -> Size`.

PRE-FIX: `visitHeritage` was called from exactly one place -- the TYPE visitor -- so a member's own `Implements IThing.Refresh` clause was never read and the whole member-level heritage form published nothing, on every member in the language. Found by the FULL-CORPUS sweep, not by a fixture: 17 of 23 missing rows on a 483-file draw, and every one of them read as a self-edge (`implements Initialize -> Initialize`) because a member that implements `IThing.Refresh` is NAMED `Refresh` -- so last-segment reduction collapses the edge onto itself. Simulated as a faithful revert by dropping `implements`/`extends` edges whose metadata records the member heritage form. Caught by vb/declaration-shapes, which expects `implements Draw -> IShape.Draw` and forbids `implements Draw -> Draw`.

RETIRED, NOT DELETED, and not because the pass stopped mattering. The declaration sweep stopped descending once it met a declaration node, so a declaration NESTED INSIDE another declaration was unreachable — on database/schema.sql that was 401 of 3,557 symbols, and the corpus's most-referenced tables were among the casualties. The pass is still worth MORE than when this mutant was written: measured under the shipped plpgsql grammar it recovers 77 declarations across 8 ProxiCall files and 375 across 79 PostgreSQL extension files. The mutant became unfixtureable because the shipped plpgsql scaffolding stopped collapsing the SMALL cases: sqld9's `RAISE EXCEPTION` body and sqld10's damaged file both parse cleanly now, so nothing in the fixture lane buries a declaration inside another declaration any more. A green-but-vacuous mutant is worse than no mutant, so it is retired here with its reason recorded, and the pass's value is pinned by corpus assertions S1/S2 in script/m60/verify-sql-resync.ts instead. RESTORE THIS MUTANT when a fixture shape exists that still buries a declaration inside another declaration under the shipped grammar — a templating shape (SQLD12 probe: `CREATE TABLE {{ ref('x') }}`) was tried and does NOT, because the declarations either side of it stay reachable and the sweep never fires. The transform below is the pre-fix behaviour and is kept so restoring it is a one-line change.
checks.detail: 4 -> 4 (RETIRED with a written-down reason: the suite has no hole here, the mutant became unfixtureable and the transform is kept so restoring it is a one-line change)

checks.description: A regression of the EXECUTE-literal pass: the analyzer only ever read declarations the PARSER handed it, so DDL a migration hands to the database as a string — `EXECUTE 'CREATE TRIGGER …'`, the dominant shape in PostgreSQL extension files — was invisible. Measured on 387 extension files the pass is worth +156 symbols and +234 relationships, and the pass reports itself in `ambiguity.executeLiterals` / `executeRecovered`. Simulated generically: everything the pass contributed is removed, keeping the main pass and the resync exactly as they are. Caught by sql/sqld11-execute-literal, whose source wraps a declaration in an EXECUTE literal and whose expectSymbols name it.

The EXECUTE-literal scanner without its comment guard. A migration that disables DDL leaves the text behind: `-- EXECUTE 'CREATE TABLE ghost (id int);'` and the same inside `/* … */`. Without skipping comments the scanner treats both as live and the analyzer publishes tables that do not exist. This is the pass's only false-positive path and it is invisible to any check that asks 'did it find the right things' — the finding is a symptom, not the defect. Simulated generically: a symbol whose own source text sits inside a comment is returned, which is what a comment-blind scanner produces. Caught by sql/sqld11-execute-literal, whose source contains both a commented-out and a live EXECUTE literal and whose expectSymbols require the ghost to be absent.

Finding X8. The `xml` and `xmlns` prefixes are bound by the Namespaces specification ITSELF, in every document, and re-binding `xml` is an error — so a well-formed file CANNOT supply them. A resolver reading only declarations therefore never resolved `xml`, the reference pass found no namespace to test for built-inness, and REFUSED the edge: 71 references over 20 corpus files, including every xml:lang in docx4j's Dublin Core schemas. The knowledge was present and unreachable — BUILTIN_NAMESPACE_URIS already held the xml namespace, consulted only when a binding existed, for the one prefix guaranteed never to bring one. Reverted generically: every reference edge whose qname uses a prefix the spec binds implicitly is deleted. Pinned by xml/xsd-implicit-xml-prefix, which declares NO xmlns:xml on purpose — adding one would make the fixture pass against the broken analyzer, which is the trap it exists to catch — and which uses the prefix xs rather than xsd so a normalising fixture would fail rather than pass.

BD2 regression: top-level edges are owned by the literal string `global` again, which isIndexArtifactName rejects as a symbol name — the exact shape that made 622 of 1432 pre-wave edges unresolvable (module-owner-bd2)

Finding X7. A references edge whose prefix is bound to a namespace the document IMPORTS points at a component declared in ANOTHER FILE. The reference pass refused it, and the refusal is right for a prefix bound to nothing — that would put a name in the graph no file supports, the M60.R10 lie. It was wrong for an imported namespace, where the document already names the file: the imports edge for the same xsd:import says where the name lives. ~108 edges lost corpus-wide, and a schema set stopped being a graph and became a pile of files. Reverted generically: every reference edge carrying resolvable === 'external' is deleted, which is the pre-fix suppression, and NO symbol is added — a reversion that also published a phantom local symbol would be testing a different defect than the one that existed. Pinned by xml/xsd-external-reference, which writes its reference BEFORE the import that authorises it (the ordinary spelling) and forbids both the phantom symbols and the still-refused unimported prefix, so a fix that simply emitted every prefixed value would fail it.

Finding X13. A BARE reference on an attribute that carries one, whose OWNER is in a declaration vocabulary, and which this document does not declare, is a REAL claim — the document says this element's type is that name — and it was being DROPPED, which is the defect this review has been closing throughout: a claim the graph cannot see. Two corpus cases are indistinguishable from inside one file. vdv-first5_0.xsd xs:includes a file declaring its OWN `date` at line 32, and `type="date"` must be that type and not XSD's built-in of the same name; cxf's calculator.xsd writes `type="xsd:int"` with no xmlns:xsd declared, which is malformed and must be refused. So the bare-built-in rule makes the first confidently WRONG and a blanket refusal makes both unresolvable for no stated reason. The fix is a FOURTH resolvability class — `unresolved`, with `ambiguousWithBuiltin` when the name is also a built-in — and the target symbol is still not published, so it adds an edge and never a phantom declaration. 413 such edges across 59 corpus files, 103 flagged ambiguous, and the most frequent unresolved targets are custom OOXML types that live in included schema files. Reverted generically: every reference edge carrying resolvable === 'unresolved' is deleted, which is the pre-fix suppression. NO symbol is added — a reversion that also published one would be testing a different defect. Pinned by xml/xsd-included-reference, which holds all three cases including the malformed undeclared prefix that must still be REFUSED, so a fix that simply emitted every bare value would fail it.

Finding X10. XML Schema's QName datatype carries the `collapse` whiteSpace facet, so a QName-typed attribute value has its whitespace runs collapsed and its ends trimmed BEFORE it is read as a name. The analyzer did not, so `type="CT_GeoHierarchyEntity "` — a trailing space, written by a human and legal, since XML only normalises tab and newline in an attribute value and leaves inner spaces alone — failed the QName parse and the reference was REFUSED. One corpus site, where a complex type declared 7 lines above went unreferenced because of one character. Reverted generically: every reference target and qname is re-read from the RAW attribute text rather than the collapsed reading the analyzer stored, which is what the pre-fix code did — the deferred pass parsed `candidate.value`, and pre-fix that WAS the raw value. Pinned by xml/xsd-qname-whitespace, which pins four spellings rather than the one that was seen in the corpus, because the facet distinguishes them: trailing, leading and a double run all collapse to the same name, and an interior space must still be refused, since collapse replaces a run with ONE space and an interior space leaves the value not a QName. A fix that merely trimmed the ends would pass a fixture pinning only the trailing case and would accept a different and wrong set of values.

Finding X6. A self-loop guard read `if (type === References || type === Imports) { if (source === target) return }`. Sound for a REFERENCE, where both ends are component names and equality is a cycle in the document. Unsound for an IMPORT, whose ends are DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING: `source` is a symbol name, `target` is a path read out of a SYSTEM identifier, and when the strings coincide they still denote a symbol and a file. `<!ENTITY cover.gif SYSTEM "cover.gif" NDATA gif>` names a real file. It was dropped ASYMMETRICALLY, which is what makes it a defect and not a policy: `extractExternalId` had already pushed the ImportInfo, so the file was in the analyzer's `imports` array and absent from its relationship graph — the analyzer contradicting itself inside one call, with the graph the part consumers read. 46 edges in the corpus. Reverted generically: every imports edge whose source equals its target is deleted, which is exactly the pre-fix suppression, and the ImportInfo is LEFT ALONE so the mutant reproduces the asymmetry rather than tidying it — a reversion that also fixed the inconsistency would not be testing the defect. Pinned by xml/dtd-self-named-external-id, whose `cover` and `cover.gif` differ by a dot and nothing else, so a normaliser that stripped path punctuation would collapse them and pass a broken analyzer.

Finding X5, and the mirror image of M60.R10. A declaration's name is a NAME; `xsl:output`'s `method` attribute names the output METHOD (`xml`/`html`/`text`) and nothing else, yet DECLARATION_NAME_ATTRIBUTE mapped `output -> method`, so `<xsl:output method="html"/>` was published as a component called `html` marked isVocabDeclaration, with `method`/`encoding`/`indent` hung off IT, and the real name `xsl:output` absent from the graph entirely. Corpus cost 182 sites over 250 files (92 as `xml`, 53 as `text`, 37 as `html`), and where a stylesheet also contained a real `<html>` element the two unrelated components shared one name. Reverted generically and SELF-CONTAINEDLY: an element that carries a `method` attribute takes that attribute's VALUE as its own name, which is the pre-fix reading, and every attribute it owned is re-owned by the renamed symbol so the whole subgraph moves with it — the second half matters, because renaming the element without re-owning its attributes leaves `method` pointing at a name that no longer exists, and the fixture's forbidden `contains html -> method` would then pass for the wrong reason. Pinned by xml/xslt-output-is-not-a-name, which contains a real `<html>` element so the collision is unavoidable rather than theoretical.
BD-shell-defined-vars regression: a read of a shell-defined name is no longer labelled, so 23 BASH_SOURCE edges look like reads of undeclared project variables again (shell-defined-vars)

BD-assigned-in-file regression: a read the file DOES assign is no longer labelled, so 14,551 of 19,417 uses edges across the corpus stop distinguishing a project variable from an environment-supplied name (assigned-in-file)

BD8b regression: a function redefinition no longer emits `overrides`, restoring the omission the ontology-coverage gate falsified — two unconnected `contains` rows for one name, and `overrides` back to zero across the ontology (redefinition-overrides)
the original state: `line_number` occurred ZERO times in the analyzer, so every json edge was stored with a NULL line while symbols carried `range` throughout (json-contract)
BD-ontology regression: a `$ref` naming another file stops emitting `imports`, restoring the omission the ontology gate falsified — 58 file-to-file $refs across 12 files (json-contract)
BD-ref-target regression: a `$ref` resolves to the bare NAME at that location rather than the LOCATION, which disagrees with the analyzer on 91% of every references edge in the corpus (json-contract)
BD-owner regression: a nested key's owner is its qualified PATH again, so its `contains` edges resolve to nothing — invisible at the top level, which is why it survived a whole wave (json-contract)
BD-array-identity regression: an array item is named by the PATH's last dot-segment, so any dotted module name truncates — `index.svelte.warnings.json` gave owners of `warnings` (json-contract)
BD-array-identity regression: an element's own keys are attributed to the ARRAY rather than to the element, so `a` reads as inside `objs` when it is inside `objs[0]` (json-contract)
BD-allOf-extends regression: `allOf` stops emitting `extends`, restoring the omission the ontology gate falsified — composition is the one JSON Schema keyword that means a superset (json-contract)
BD-allOf-extends regression: only the intra-document `$ref` form composes, so an `allOf` naming a sibling file stops emitting `extends` — the exact subset bug, 3 corpus edges (json-contract)
an edge is emitted whose source is not a symbol in the file — the class BD2 removed and the one every bash fixture's universal forbid set convicts

M60.P1 regression, ARM A: reverts the parameter TYPE slice from the parameter's NAME node to its DECLARATOR node. A `reference_declarator`'s text is `& name` and its start index points at the `&`, so slicing at the declarator deletes the pointer/ref operator and publishes `const std::string` for `const std::string& name` and `const char` for `const char* format`. Not cosmetic: those are different C++ types that overload differently, and the same slice is the override-matching KEY (buildParamSig), so `virtual void f(Widget&)` and `virtual void f(Widget)` also hashed alike before the fix.

M60.P1 regression, ARM B: drops every DEFAULTED parameter. In this grammar a defaulted parameter is an `optional_parameter_declaration` — a DIFFERENT node type from a required `parameter_declaration` — so a walk that handles only the required one silently loses `double scale = 1.0` while looking correct on every undefaulted signature. The class is corpus-wide and invisible to a name/type pin that happens to sample an all-required signature.

M60.P1 regression, ARM C: publishes a deduced-return function's `auto` instead of the type after the `->`. The pre-fix read took the declaration's `type` field, which for `auto label() const -> std::string` is literally `auto` — a name that resolves to nothing, in the one field whose whole job is to name a type. Trailing return types are not exotic: they are how `decltype(auto)` and every deduced-return function is written.

M60.P1 regression, ARM D: drops `decorators` from every non-callable declaration, keeping it only for functions. `static constexpr int kAxes = 2;` carries exactly as much modifier information as `virtual double area() const = 0;`, so a payload field that answers for one of them and not the other is a field a consumer cannot rely on. A distinct arm from the others because it is a SCOPE restriction, not a wrong value: the function-branch values are all still correct, which is what makes it survive a fixture that only samples methods.

M60.P1 regression, ARM E: removes the one step that looks BELOW the declaration. `override` and `final` are `virtual_specifier` nodes in this grammar, children of the declarator rather than of the declaration, so a scan of the declaration's own tokens finds `virtual` and misses `override` — and `override` is the modifier that answers the question a reader actually has of an override edge.
