It is also the arm most likely to survive review, because the declaration-level modifiers are all still present.

M60.P1 regression, ARM F: scans only the DECLARATION for modifiers and not its DECLARATOR. A method's trailing `const` and its `override`/`final` `virtual_specifier`s are children of the `function_declarator`, so this arm drops `const` from every const method and every override — while leaving `static`/`virtual`/`explicit` intact, because those DO sit on the declaration. It is the arm most likely to pass review, since the modifiers a reader checks first are all still there, and `const` is on essentially every getter in a C++ corpus, so the loss is large and the signal is small.

Z22 regression: a CONTAINER declared inside an executable body stops being anonymous, so its declarations are handed to the ENCLOSING container again — `const Local = struct { pub fn helper(v: T) void }` inside a method of `Host` publishes `helper` as a Method owned by `Host` with a `contains Host -> helper` edge. Measured by the ownership verifier (script/m14/tmp/zigw-ownership.ts, whose key IS the owner: the differential cannot see this class because its coverage match ignores the source). Caught by zig/kinds-and-owners' forbidSymbols (`helper`, `limit`) and forbidRelationships on the two `contains` shapes.

Z30 regression: the `imports` twin edges stop being published, so every module dependency reverts to living only under `references` — the state 16 other lanes and the graph engine are not in. A module path is not a declaration name (176 of 394 distinct targets in 400 corpus files contain a separator), so `imports` is the only type where the fact is expressible. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' expectRelationships on `imports ../helper.zig`, and by the imports gate, which counts the type by name.

Z32 regression: the CONSTRUCTION half of `instantiates` goes away — `Point{ .x = 0, .y = 0 }` publishes no instantiation edge, which is the class ZIG.GAP.3 has wanted since it was written. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' expectRelationships on `instantiates Point` and `instantiates Inner` (the qualified head), and by the instantiation gate, which counts the two classes separately so a regression in one is attributable.

Z32 regression: the GENERIC TYPE APPLICATION half of `instantiates` goes away — `Scaled(u8, 4)`, a call to an in-file `fn ... type`, publishes no instantiation edge. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' expectRelationships on `instantiates Scaled`, and by the instantiation gate.

Z33 regression: `exports` relationships stop being published, so the module's public API surface exists only in the result's export ARRAY and never in the graph — 1,584 file-scope `pub`/`export` declarations over 400 corpus files, invisible to any query that reads relationships. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' expectRelationships on three export targets, and by the exports gate, which is bidirectional so it also catches the array drifting from the edges.

Z35 regression: a NAMESPACE IMPORT BINDING stops minting a symbol — `const std = @import("std")` becomes an edge and no name, so the module's own namespace is missing its most common declaration (1,458 bindings in 400 corpus files) and a `pub const X = @import(...)` re-export names a binding the index cannot resolve. Reconstructed by dropping the symbols the analyzer marks `zigImportBinding`, which is why that marker exists rather than a name list. Caught by zig/relationship-classes' expectSymbols (`helper`, `reexported`) and by the fixture runner's export invariant, a general check this lane did not have to write.

Z29 regression: the LHS test goes back to "the first named child of type `identifier`", which is not the LHS when the left side is a field expression — in `exe.stack_size = stack_size` the first identifier child is the VALUE, so the analyzer declares the read to be a definition and publishes no `uses` for it. One row in 1,200 corpus files (zig/build.zig), a real read of a file-scope constant. Caught by the differential's bare-read truth, whose own copy of this predicate was fixed twice in the same wave (Z24, Z25) before the third copy — in the analyzer — was noticed.

Z28 regression: the container-field extraction goes back to requiring a name shorter than 50 characters, so real field declarations vanish from the index again — 14 of 27,004 in 1,200 corpus files (0.05%), including a 74-character LSP capability flag. This is a LOSS class, so a count of published symbols cannot show it: the only instrument that convicts it is one that asks what SHOULD be published. Caught by zig/kinds-and-owners' expectSymbols (`supports_workspace_did_change_configuration_dynamic_registration`), and by the `contains` gate, whose derived-and-unpublished direction reports it as MISSING.

Z26 regression: a `function_signature` — a function-pointer TYPE, which has no `declarator` field in this grammar — goes back on the declaration path, so the name-picking takes whatever identifier comes first under the node and publishes a METHOD that does not exist: the return type (`contains Sort -> ComparisonResult`) or a qualified segment of a parameter type (`contains Options -> apprt` from `*apprt.ClipboardRequest`). Caught by zig/kinds-and-owners' forbidSymbols (`ComparisonResult`, `Order`, `apprt`) and forbidRelationships on the two `contains` shapes. Measured by the `contains` gate (script/m14/tmp/zigw-contains.ts), which is BIDIRECTIONAL — it also asks whether a justifiable owner is missing, which the ownership verifier cannot.

#924 (M60, the kotlin row of the name-surface class) regression: the quoting syntax goes back to being part of the NAME — `fun `in`(x: Int)` publishes `in` instead of `in`, `param.`in`(1)` calls `in`, and the declaration's `contains` target carries the backticks again. Faithful by construction: the pre-fix spellings are re-derived from the fixture's own backtick runs, and only whole identifier SEGMENTS are rewritten, so `Parameters.`in`` is restored while an unrelated `insert` is not. Caught by kotlin/quoted-name-surface-924, whose forbidSymbols name all three quoted spellings and whose `targetEndsWith: "`"` pins cover the containment, call, read and reference surfaces as a CLASS rather than as a sample. NOTE what this mutant cannot catch, stated because the lane shipped it: the repair's ORACLE half was dead (the strip call sat inside a `//` comment) and every fixture in the suite stayed green — a fixture reads the analyzer, and the analyzer was the correct side. That state is caught by F9-PROBE-KT-QUOTED-NAME-924-ORACLE (script/m14/verify-probe-battery.ts), the only instrument that asserts the oracle's spelling directly.

ERROR RECOVERY: the walk STOPS at the first recovery node. Nothing counts symbols-per-file against a floor, so a silently half-analysed document reads as analysed — and the module symbol spans the whole root, so a truncated document still has an identity and every visible count stays plausible. Svelte makes it sharper than html: an unclosed `{#if}` does not clip the damage to the broken line, the parser's ERROR span swallows the REST OF THE FILE, so the tail is valid markup inside the error region. Measured on the real corpus, 2.44% of files carry recovery nodes, and when one does what follows is usually good content — a stopping walk discards the majority of a damaged document. Modelled by dropping every relationship and symbol at or after the FIRST reported error, reading the analyzer's own diagnostic rather than the engine's so the mutated result still looks correctly reported. Caught by svelte/error-recovery, whose `Beta` at L12 and `uses shared` at L12 sit after the error and inside its span.

D12 obligation 1 of 2: the MEMBER-READ carriers are dropped. `bind:`, `class:` and `style:` each read a component member in the template, which is the S1 case, and every one was silent before the ruling — roughly 1,857 corpus occurrences including `bind:value` at 581, the most common attribute interaction in the corpus. Removing them drops the component's primary data-flow surface while the document still looks analysed. Selective on the `carrierDirective` provenance flag rather than on a blanket `uses` filter: a blanket drop is caught by a dozen unrelated fixtures and would prove nothing about D12, and the first version of this mutant used a `metadata.context` marker that only the CALL edges carry, so it SURVIVED. Caught by svelte/directive-carriers.

D12 obligation 2 of 2: the FRAMEWORK-INVOKED carriers are dropped. `use:`, `transition:`, `in:`, `out:` and `animate:` are call sites on exactly the argument that made `on:click` one under D8 — Svelte calls an action on mount and a transition on state change by the same mechanism. Their silence was an internal inconsistency rather than a position, and the mutant restores it. Selective by metadata marker so the `on:` handler edges survive and a failure is attributable to this family rather than to the D8 pass. Caught by svelte/directive-carriers.

D7: rune invocations are dropped. A named function handed to a rune that INVOKES its argument ($effect, $effect.pre, $effect.root, $effect.untracked, $derived.by, $host) is a call site, so a component that runs `fn` on every effect tick must say so in its graph — before the ruling these six forms emitted nothing, because the delegate suppresses the rune and the argument is an ordinary identifier no edge was made for. Selective rather than blanket: a blanket 'drop every calls edge' would be caught by any fixture and would prove nothing about D7. Only edges carrying the rune-pass marker are removed, so the js-delegate call inside `$effect(inlineCall())` and the D8 template-handler call both survive, which is what makes a failure attributable to the ruling rather than to the delegate. Caught by svelte/rune-invocations.

GO38 regression: a type declared INSIDE A FUNCTION BODY stops being published — the symbol, its member symbols and its `contains` edges all go. LocalsAreNotSymbols (C# M12.07 / Swift M12.21) excludes a function-local var/const, and the family's stated exception is nim's own: 'THE ONE EXCEPTION IS AN OBJECT/ENUM/FIELD DECLARATION, WHICH IS A SYMBOL BECAUSE THE OBJECT OWNS IT.' The pre-fix walk `continue`d on every function and method, so it never reached a local type. The silence was not neutral — `extractDeclaredTypeRefs` already walks bodies and already attributed a local type's field types to that type, so the lane published `references Local -> Host` whose SOURCE named no symbol at all. Found by the round-6 `contains` truth, which derives membership from the DECLARATION side and therefore reports an unpublished type as MISSING instead of being invisible on both sides (22 memberships in 200 go-tools files). Reconstructed from the output: a struct symbol whose range falls inside a function symbol's range is a function-local type, so it and its members and its contains edges are removed. Caught by go/local-type-declaration, which also FORBIDS publishing the function-local var/const — the other half of the same contract, without which this mutant's opposite would pass too.

GO36 regression: a type ALIAS's field types attribute to the `global` pseudo-source again. `resolveSource` recognised `type_spec` only, so `type Alias = struct{ Q Inner }` found no enclosing declaration and emitted `global -> Inner` — an edge no consumer can navigate back from, since `global` names nothing. This is the second half of GO31a (which taught the embedding pass to accept `type_alias` and left the declared-type resolver behind), found by the round-6 `references` truth: 16 MISSING + 16 UNEXPLAINED rows over go-tools's 1,931 files. Reconstructed from the output: an edge whose source is a type ALIAS struct that owns members is re-sourced to `global`. Caught by go/round5-surfaces, which expects `references Alias -> Holder` and forbids the `global` spelling for BOTH alias-owned targets (the embedded `Inner` and the named `Holder`, the latter added because the lane's per-set convention would otherwise let the embedded field's edge satisfy the pin on its own).

GOD9 regression: the channel-op pass gates on `containingFunction &&`, and findContainingGoFunction returns undefined for a FUNC LITERAL, so every channel read inside a package-scope closure is DISCARDED. Reconstructed from the output by dropping the `uses` edges whose source is `global` and whose marker is go_channel_operation — that is exactly the set the pre-fix truthiness gate could not produce, and `global` is only ever a channel-op source through the fallback. This mutant is also the reason the god8/god9 channel rule is worth pinning: the analyzer contradicted ITSELF here, publishing the same physical read through the selector/identifier passes as `global -> c` while the channel pass threw it away. Caught by go/closure-channel-read, whose FORBID rows (`local`, `l`, `ch`, a call-result receive, and a `for range` over a channel) mean the mutant's opposite — a pass that published every operand — would not pass this fixture either.

D1 revert: `line_number` is not set on any relationship. It is a PRODUCT field — the indexer stores it (src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts:2789) and the address surfaces serve call-site positions from it (src/intelligence/graph/line-address.ts) — so this is the shape the lane was in for every one of its 1,784 edges: navigable to a symbol, but not to a LINE. Reverted generically by deleting the field from every edge.

D2 revert: the trailing assignment operator is left in the captured name. The grammar's `word` node spans `CGO_ENABLED?` for `?=` but only `CC` for `:=`, so the two spellings disagree. Measured: 55 symbols named `CGO_ENABLED?`/`BUILD_TAGS+`, and 112 edge ends that dangled by construction because every reference names the clean identifier.

D3 revert: references are collected only beneath a `variable_assignment` or a `rule`, so a bare top-level expression contributes nothing. `$(foreach t,… $(eval $(call mk,$(t))))` — the idiom nomad/GNUmakefile uses to reify its package targets — is a `function_call` directly under `makefile`; the corpus has one such site and it produced zero edges.

D4 revert: `$(VAR:.c=.o)` is a `substitution_reference`, a SIBLING of `variable_reference` and not a child of it. Reading only the latter loses every substitution reference — 9 in this corpus, and the one in the fixture is the whole point of that fixture.

D5 revert: `export NAME` with no `=` wraps a `list` and has no assignment node anywhere, so it is the only place that name appears. Ignoring the list form makes the export invisible entirely — 22 `export` lines in this corpus, of which the bare form is a share.

D6 revert: the include edge is sourced at a literal `makefile` instead of this file's module node. With a constant source every makefile that includes `hooks` produces the SAME edge, so two files cannot be told apart in the graph and no include can be attributed to a file.

D7 revert: the BUILTIN / EXTERNAL / PROJECT split is collapsed, every reference becomes `uses`. A variable this file declares then leaves the reference graph, which is how a real declaration gets demoted; and a prerequisite that is only a FILE is published as a project-internal reference, asserting a declaration that does not exist. Measured over the corpus: 231 file-path, 187 external-variable and 160 builtin edge ends are on the wrong side of this line.

D8 revert: only the FIRST `prerequisites` node of a rule is read. The grammar emits one node per `|`-separated group, so an order-only list is a second node — 172 order-only prerequisites in this corpus are invisible if only the first group is taken.

D9 revert: a `$(foreach VAR,…)` binder is labelled `external` instead of `local_binding`. It is neither an external variable nor a project declaration — it is a local introduced by the loop, and pooling it with the 187 genuinely-external names is what makes the `uses` class unreadable.

D10 revert: a computed include (`include $(shell …)`) is dropped. Its target is a `shell_function` node, not the `function_call` an implementer would reach for first, and the target is not knowable at parse time — so the EXPRESSION must be recorded and flagged. A dropped include is invisible; an unresolved one is a fact.

D11 revert: a keyword reaching the name-capture path is accepted as a name. `export` reached it in boundary/Makefile and appeared as the target of six edges — an edge to a keyword is an edge to nothing, and it also means the exported variable was never declared.
D12 revert: a `define` declares a `constant`. A `$(call NAME)` that resolves to a constant is a callee that cannot be called, and the graph's call edges then point at values.

D13 revert: the module node does not `contains` its declarations. GNU Make has exactly one declaration level, so the file node is the only place containment can live — without it, "what does this Makefile declare?" is unanswerable and the module symbol has no outgoing edge at all.

D14 revert: only `export VAR` lines produce exports and a buildable target does not. A target IS the file's public surface — an including makefile invokes it by name — so this is the shape the lane shipped with `exports: []` hardcoded, where the answer to "what does this Makefile offer?" was nothing at all.

D15 revert: a `$(NAME)` prerequisite is recorded under its wrapper text rather than normalised to NAME. The dependency is on the expansion, so the edge target must be the variable — otherwise `all: $(OBJ)` publishes a target named `$(OBJ)` that nothing declares and the reference to OBJ is lost.

D16 revert: `$@`/`$<`/`$^` are labelled `builtin` and `$$?` is too. An automatic variable is a Make builtin read, and `$$?` is the SHELL's exit-status variable because `$$` is Make's escaped dollar — calling it a Make builtin is a category error that hides 212 automatic and 11 shell edge ends inside the builtin bucket.

D18 revert: a rule whose TARGET is an expression publishes no prerequisite edges. `$(BIN): $(OBJS) | builddir` declares no literal target name, so the pre-fix code iterated the empty list of literal targets and dropped the whole rule's dependencies — first group and order-only alike (405 corpus edges). Found by script/m12/make-contract-probe.ts, a gate that had existed for this lane and had never been run; a check that is never executed cannot report the defect it was written for.

D17 revert: only the `$(NAME)` expansion form is normalised, so `${NAME}` keeps its raw wrapper. `${VAR}` is GNU Make's SECOND expansion form and it is common — 68 occurrences across 14 of the 99 corpus files — and every one of those prerequisites was published as `uses target -> ${VAR}` while the variable it names was declared elsewhere, so the same fact appeared twice under two spellings and the wrapper form dangled. Found by the corpus differential, not by reading the code: it was the last two rows of a 5,035-edge comparison. This mutant needs the SOURCE: the fix normalises the target during extraction, so by the time a result-level transform runs there is no `${...}` left to rewrite and a naive re-wrap is a silent no-op — the same instrument failure that left swift/drop-container-subscript-uses surviving. It therefore re-wraps only those edges whose own line really contains the brace form.

R1 regression, the half that is computable from the analyzer RESULT: a member whose container names no DECLARATION is not extracted again — `const Named = class Inner { usesHelper() {} }` loses both the member symbol and its payload. class-expression-members kills it on the usesHelper/Inner ownerName pins. The other half of the defect (the variable path not descending into a class VALUE, which also lost the members of an ANONYMOUS class expression and of a class expression assigned by assignment) is NOT reproducible here: the container's kind is not recoverable from a ParseResult, so those members are indistinguishable from object-literal members after the fact — the FIXTURE carries them via expectSymbols on m@Anon and m@Assigned instead.

M1 regression: restores the implements-only structural override arm — a class EXTENDING an in-file base emits no overrides unless the member carries the optional `override` keyword, so the majority shape (class Sub extends Base { run(){} }) loses the edge the oracle derives as truth; class-extends-overrides pins Sub.run/SubKeyword.run/SubTransitive.run

R12 regression: a parameter stops shadowing a same-named file-level symbol, so the reference pass resolves the body read to the wrong declaration. With `interface Deps { root: string }` in the file, `function f(root: string) { return root }` publishes `f->root` again — the graph recording a function as referencing an interface property it never touches, purely because its own parameter had that name. The pass resolves by NAME, and it already suppressed locally-bound names through `locals` (destructuring patterns and local declarators); a parameter was simply missing, and the fix belongs at the references guard rather than in `locals` because `locals` also gates the `uses` edge, where an edge to a parameter is wanted (interp-uses pins `greet -> name`). The transform re-adds a `references` edge from every symbol to any of its own parameter names that also exists as a file-level symbol — the exact pre-fix shape. parameter-shadows-file-symbol kills it, and its positive pins (`usesConst -> root`, `callsHelper -> helper`, `annotates -> Deps`) are what stop a fix that over-suppresses from passing.

R11 regression: CommonJS `require()` stops being a module dependency, and the module loader starts being published as a call instead — the two halves of the same construct, which is why the twin skips the bare `require` callee while still recording the dependency. The transform drops every `imports` edge carrying `meta.isRequire` and re-publishes each as a `calls` edge to a function named `require`, which is what the analyzer did before the port. It covers all four require spellings at once — the plain call, a destructuring binding, a bare-identifier binding, and TypeScript's `import m = require("m")` whose path lives in an `import_require_clause` rather than the statement's `source` field — because the last one is the shape most likely to regress silently: reading only the `source` field skips it with no error. `imports` is the second-largest edge class in this lane (2,692 edges over 600 tracked files) so a silently missing dependency is a hole in impact analysis. commonjs-require-module-graph kills it, including the exact-count pins that separate a legitimate member call named `require` from a spurious one.

R10 regression: a declaration inside a function body inherits the enclosing class or namespace as its owner again, so `contains Report->helper` — the graph claims the class has a member that belongs to a closure inside one of its methods. Two causes, both restored by re-attributing every ownerless declaration to the file's containers: the eager scope pop in extractClass/extractInterface/extractEnum, and `getOwnerInfo()` being asked about lexical nesting that an accumulating resource stack cannot answer. The transform adds a containment edge from every container to every ownerless function/type/interface symbol, which is the observable shape of the pre-fix output; the lane's new independent contains oracle is the instrument that found it (8 false edges over 200 files of an external corpus). declaration-in-body-is-local kills it on the forbidRelationships pins, and its positives — three ordered members, and a body-local type alias still containing its own members — are what stop a fix that simply suppressed ownership from passing.

R8 regression: bodyless function DECLARATIONS stop emitting. `declare function f(): T` parses to `function_signature`, not `function_declaration`, and the pre-fix analyzer had no reference to that node type at all — while the spec listed it as handled_verified and the coverage gate was satisfied by a fixture that merely PARSED one. Every exported function in a .d.ts was therefore invisible: no symbol, no call edge, no complexity, no api-contract row. The transform reproduces that by dropping every function symbol that is marked as an ambient declaration, and it also clears the flag itself, because pre-fix nothing could have set it (the `declare` keyword is not a child of the node; it sits on a wrapping ambient_declaration). ambient-function-signature kills it.

R7 regression: an object-literal get/set pair stops collapsing to one property. The fix keeps the LAST accessor of a pair; the defect emitted one symbol per accessor, and because containment emits one `contains` row per member symbol, the same edge appeared twice. This transform reconstructs that output by giving every object-literal PROPERTY member a second declaration — the observable shape of the pre-fix analyzer. It cannot read the AST, so it cannot know which properties were accessor pairs, and it therefore over-applies: the point is that object-literal-accessor-pair's exact-count pin (contains o->size equals 1) MUST fail, which is the only assertion in the suite that can fail on a duplicate at all, since expectSymbols is a >=1 match and passes happily with both symbols present.

Restores the pre-fix signal scan, which read child_process only off an import_statement or an `import ... = require(...)` clause. A CommonJS `require("child_process")` — a CALL, not an import — no longer arms the rule, so a bare exec-family call in such a file loses its command_injection sink and no flow into it can be reported: the false NEGATIVE direction, which costs a real vulnerability rather than adding noise. taint-sink-require-child-process kills it (a bare execFileSync whose only evidence is the require form). The transform is the exact inverse of the fix: a bare exec-family sink is kept when the file's import list already proves child_process, and stripped when the ONLY evidence was the call.

H1 regression: restores bare-name/bare-LEAF sink matching — RegExp.prototype.exec, a project-local execute() and the project's own spawn() are reported as command_injection / sql_injection again, and because the store multiplies sources by sinks, one req.body read beside any .exec() manufactures a persisted command-injection flow. taint-sink-receiver kills it on the notIncludesVuln pins (the exact-snippet pins cannot catch a rebuilt snippet, which is why the vulnerability_type pins are in the fixture)

M5 regression: an arrow/function-VALUED variable loses its API contract again — the dominant handler shape (Next.js/Astro/Express arrow consts) reports no path while the byte-identical function declaration still does; arrow-contracts-and-exports expectApiContractPaths pins arrowGet/arrowPost
M4 regression: an anonymous default export emits an `exports` edge to `default` again — a target no symbol in this or any other file can own; arrow-contracts-and-exports forbidRelationships kills it

M8 regression: linesOfCode counts non-empty lines again, so the same source reports a different LOC as .ts than as .js (measured 37 vs 43 on the pinned fixture); arrow-contracts-and-exports expectMetadata.linesOfCode catches it

M3 regression, the dangerous half: removes the per-function REBINDING while keeping the boundary removal — the payload walk started at a symbol and charged every call below it to that symbol, so a nested function's or object-literal method's calls were ALSO listed on the enclosing symbol (enclosing lists helper besides inner; mixed lists persist besides save). qualified-calls-nested-scope kills it on the notIncludes pins, which is the only shape that can tell 'omitted' from 'double-counted'

M7 regression: restores the bare-name-only builtin table — node:fs/promises, node:test, stream/promises and every other subpath Node ships resolve to external:<specifier> again, so the index claims npm packages named 'fs/promises' and 'test' (node-builtin-subpaths meta.resolvedPath pins catch it; lodash/merge stays external in both, so the pin set cannot be satisfied by classifying everything external)

ER-D35 regression: treats EVERY macro in remote-module position as `?MODULE` and substitutes this file's module, inventing a self-call that is nowhere in the source. Measured on otp/lib/debugger/test/line_number_SUITE.erl and otp/lib/dialyzer/test/r9c_SUITE_data/src/inets/httpd_acceptor.erl, where `?FILE_MODULE:acceptor(A,B,C,D)` was reported as `httpd_acceptor:acceptor`; 922 fabricated edges over the corpus. macro-module-er3 FORBIDS the self-call and the bare leaf, while dispatch-er3 keeps the legitimate `?MODULE` self-dispatch pinned

ER-D34 regression: reverts `-module(?MACRO)` to requiring a bare atom under the attribute, so a module that names itself through a macro emits NO module symbol and the file falls back to being owned by its path. Measured on otp/lib/kernel/test/file_SUITE.erl (`-module(?FILE_SUITE).`), the only such file in the 4,326-file corpus; the attribute carries a macro_call_expr, never an atom. modname-macro-er3 REQUIRES the module symbol and its macro reference

ER-D34 regression, the subtle half: mints the module symbol under the MACRO's own name (MODNAME) instead of what it expands to (modname_macro_er3). Every consumer of a module symbol — exports, imports, cross-module calls — would then look for a module no compile can produce. modname-macro-er3 pins the module name AND meta.expandsTo

ER-D33 regression: `contains` carries the CONSTRUCT's line (range.startLine) instead of the NAME's line. Found by the 400-file corpus draw, missed by the 150-file one: otp/lib/snmp/src/manager/snmpm_net_if.erl defines worker/4 in two -ifdef/-else branches, so the -define( keyword sits on 208 and 219 while the macro names are on 209 and 220. line-owner-er3 FORBIDS the construct lines and REQUIRES the name lines for a macro, a function-like macro, a record and a type

ER-D32 regression: reverts the owner fallback for MODULES-scope declarations to the bare pre-pass module name, so in a module-less include fragment (no -module at all - OTP's own merl examples are written that way) macros lose their owner entirely while the function beside them keeps the file-path owner. fragment-er3 REQUIRES the macro's contains edge, which only exists when the macro is owned

EX-A14 regression (the pre-fix state): a `@callback`/`@macrocallback` declaration publishes no symbol at all, so a module that declares a behaviour surface with no `def` (Callback.Probe) has no trace of it in the index. Caught by the callback-declarations fixture's symbol pins.

EX-A14 over-correction: a `@callback` mints its OWN symbol instead of sharing the function merge key, so `@callback load(t)` + `def load(x)` publish TWO symbols for one function — ids the index (`${fileId}:${name}:${startLine}`) cannot even keep apart. Caught by the fixture's expectSymbolCount pair.

EX-A14 regression: the bodyless-def detection is read backwards, so EVERY `def` is marked isDeclaration (and every merged symbol keeps the flag). A definition that claims to be a declaration is a false statement the store persists in brain_symbol.is_declaration (#612). Caught by the fixture's forbidSymbols entries on `load`, `twice` and the protocol implementation's `size`.

EX-A14 regression: the declaration symbols survive but the TYPED SPEC does not — callbackSpec / isCallbackDeclaration / hasCallbackSpec are stripped, so the index knows a callback exists but not its contract. Differential-invisible (no edge moves), so only the fixture can hold it.

EX-A15 regression: a PARENTHESIZED operator definition publishes the EX-D9 placeholder instead of the operator name, and two of them in one module merge into one row (measured pre-fix: `expected 1 symbol(s) named Unknown; got 2` on fixture paren-operator-forms, because `defmacro (..)` and `def (---)(l, r)` both fell through). Caught by the fixture's operator-name pins, its placeholder count pin, and its placeholder-kind forbid.

EX-A16 regression: `metadata.isDeclaration` is stripped, which is the ONE key the pool worker carries to the store phase — the top-level field alone does not survive the worker's symbol reconstruction, so brain_symbol.is_declaration goes NULL for every elixir declaration. Caught by the callback-declarations fixture's meta.isDeclaration pins; the SQL round-trip (script/m14/tmp/elixir-store-roundtrip.ts) is the seam gate.
EX-A17: module-attribute VALUE edges removed (instantiates + calls raised from a compile-time attribute value) — the pre-fix state, 21 attribute sites in 250 files of ash with no dependency edge
EX-A17: the attribute's own name emitted as a call (`@section` -> calls->section) — a lowercase phantom callee naming no function, the regression the attribute-value relaxation invites
EX-A18: multi-alias members that are lowercase identifiers (function aliases) publish no `references` edge — `alias Helper.{make, name}` named no dependency at all
EX-A18: a bare call through a lowercase function alias keeps the bare name (`calls->make`) instead of the alias target (`calls->Helper.make`) — the edge then names no module and matches no symbol

M14.6 regression: `use constant { A => 1, B => 2 }` goes back to declaring NOTHING. fatCommaKeys' `else if (node.type === "anonymous_hash_expression")` branch was unreachable — the caller passes the use_statement and findChildByType is shallow, so the list one level down was never found. The bare `use constant A => 1` form kept working, which is why the code looked tested. Measured on mojo: 7 constants lost in Mojo::Util (the PC_* table) and 6 in Mojo::WebSocket (WS_*). Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' expectSymbols {MAX} and {MIN} (expectSymbolCount pins PI at exactly 1, so the bare form cannot go quiet either).

M14.6 regression: a double-quoted `use` argument loses its items again. `use feature "class"` and `use lib "./t/lib"` are interpolated_string_literal, which neither perlWordValues nor perlArgumentNodes accepted, so the import survived with items:[]. Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' expectImports for module `feature` (items [class]) and module `lib` (items [./t/lib]) — the matcher compares the items array, so an empty list cannot satisfy it.

M14.6 regression: `no strict` / `no warnings` go back to being dependency imports. `no` is the unnamed first token of the same use_statement node type as `use`, so the pre-review rule read them as module loads and put an edge on a file that loads nothing. Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' forbidImports for module `strict` and its forbidRelationships {type: imports, target: strict}.

M14.6 regression: `use 5.010` goes back to being an import. A version requirement is language metadata (perlVersion / perlVersions), never a module named "5.010". Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' forbidImports for module `5.010`.

M14.6 regression: `use constant` emits an import named "constant" and declares no Constant symbols — the pre-review shape exactly. Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' forbidImports for module `constant` AND its expectSymbols {PI}/{MAX}/{MIN}, so the mutant cannot pass by being quiet about the import alone.

M14.6 regression: `require Runtime::Only` stops being an import. A runtime require IS a dependency; the pre-review rule only read `use`, and mojo alone has 39 require sites. Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' expectImports {module: Runtime::Only} and perl/inheritance's import pins.

M14.6 regression: only `@EXPORT` is read, so `@EXPORT_OK` and `%EXPORT_TAGS` stop producing exports — the pre-review shape, which lost the whole optional half of every Exporter module in a corpus. Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' expectExports for gamma, delta and all (and by the harness's exports invariant, since `all` resolves to no symbol once its name is gone from @EXPORT_TAGS).

M14.6 regression: `use Mojo::Base -base` names no parent at all. The pre-review rule skipped every option-bearing form, so the flag-only spelling — used by every Mojo Controller and Plugin — produced no extends edge: 53 of mojo's 118 inheritance sites. The class being subclassed is Mojo::Base ITSELF. Caught by perl/inheritance's expectRelationships {extends, MojoStyle -> Base, line_number 8}.
M14.6 regression: the option token of `use parent -norequire, 'Base'` becomes a base class. Caught by perl/inheritance's forbidRelationships {extends, UsesParent -> norequire}.

M14.6 regression: a class naming ITSELF as its base emits the edge. `package SelfNamed; use Mojo::Base 'SelfNamed';` is a real self-reference in the source and a useless edge in a graph. The guard compares FULLY QUALIFIED names; a leaf comparison also fired for `package Foo::Bar` over a different `Other::Bar` and deleted 7 legitimate override edges across mojo and plack. Caught by perl/inheritance's forbidRelationships {extends, SelfNamed -> SelfNamed} and {overrides, SelfNamed.run -> SelfNamed.run}.

M14.6 regression: the BLOCK form of `package` leaks past its closing brace, so a file-scope sub is emitted as a method of the block's package. Proved by EXECUTING perl 5.34, not by reading the grammar: after `package Outer { }`, __PACKAGE__ is `main`. Caught by perl/package-block-scope's forbidRelationships {contains, Outer -> after_block} and forbidSymbols {after_block, ownerName Outer} — the statement form on line 5 must STILL change the package, so the mutant cannot be caught by simply never tracking one.

M14.6 (#863) regression: the dead `childForFieldName("parameters")` lookup returns, so no sub publishes a parameter list again. The pinned grammar declares no `parameters` field; a signature is the `signature` FIELD of mandatory/optional/slurpy_parameter children. The pre-review lane shipped 0 parameters across 29,640 symbols on 5,866 files. Caught by perl/signatures-and-attributes' expectParameters for mandatory, optional and slurpy, and perl/core-oo-class-role's expectParameters for the two constructors.

M14.6 regression: the grammar's `attributes` field is not read, so `decorators` is never emitted at all — the pre-review state, where the whole attribute surface was absent for every language that has it. Caught by perl/signatures-and-attributes' expectDecorators for lvalue_attr (lvalue, method) and prototyped (prototype).

M14.6 regression: `class_statement` and `role_statement` produce no symbol at all, so `class Point` / `role Greeter` vanish and their methods become ownerless functions. `field $x` / `field $y` go with them. Caught by perl/core-oo-class-role's expectSymbols {Point, class} and {Greeter, trait} and its expectRelationships {contains, Point -> sum} — an implementation that only stopped reading class statements, but left the block walking intact, still fails the contains pins.

M14.6 regression: `field $x` inside a `class` block is emitted as a bare variable with no owner instead of a Property owned by the class — the same concept as a Moose `has` attribute. Caught by perl/core-oo-class-role's expectSymbols {x, kind property, ownerName Point} and {contains, Point -> x}.

M14.6 regression: the builtin suppression set goes back to its hand-maintained size, which was missing exactly 10 words — say, system, accept, chr and fc among them. Those are core named operators, so each one emitted a `calls` edge to a symbol that cannot exist. The set is now the grammar's own fixed op-token sets intersected with perl 5.38's opcode.h, so it cannot drift from the parser that reads it. Caught by perl/builtins-and-branches' five forbidRelationships (say, system, accept, chr, fc) with bless as the control that must STAY suppressed.

M14.6 regression: cyclomaticComplexity collapses to 1. The pre-review counter named six node types the pinned grammar does not declare (if_statement, unless_statement, while_statement, until_statement, foreach_statement, ternary_expression), so only for_statement and conditional_expression ever fired and the metric was 1 for almost every real file. This grammar spells them conditional_statement, elsif, loop_statement, cstyle_for_statement, postfix_conditional_expression and conditional_expression. Caught by perl/builtins-and-branches' expectMetadata {cyclomaticComplexity: 11}.

M14.6 regression: `__PACKAGE__->new` emits `instantiates __PACKAGE__.constructor` — a type no source line supports, since __PACKAGE__ is a compile-time token for the CURRENT package, not a class. Caught by perl/magic-invocant's forbidRelationships {instantiates, target __PACKAGE__.constructor} and {instantiates, global -> main.constructor}: line 1 has no package in scope, so the token names nothing derivable and the edge must be omitted rather than invented.

M14.6 regression: `with 'Role::One'` and `use role 'Role::Two'` emit no implements edge, leaving a composed role an undeclared dependency. Caught by perl/imports-and-exports' expectRelationships {implements, Impl -> One, line_number 23} and {implements, Impl -> Two, line_number 24}.

M14.6 regression: the first-parent override guess claims source confidence. `overrides` is the lane's ONLY guessed relationship — inferred from the first parent at 0.5, and a perl class may inherit from several bases with only the first consulted. A 0.5 edge can never clear a 0.7 structural floor, so classifyEvidenceTier labels it `inferred` with no special case. Caught by perl/inheritance's expectRelationships {overrides, UsesParent.run -> Base.run, confidence 0.5, line_number null}: a mutant that raises the confidence fails the pin, and one that keeps it but adds a line fails the line_number:null assertion.

M14.6 regression: every source-derived edge loses its line. calls, instantiates, implements and extends are all WRITTEN in the source; only contains (membership) and the guessed overrides ride no line. The analyzer's OWN recovery diagnostic is dropped, leaving the engine to report alone. The error-recovery contract is REPORTED / BYPASSED / KEEP PUBLISHING, and before this the toml analyzer pushed no diagnostics at all, so the reported half was entirely the engine's reached through a caller — a contract resting on someone else's completeness. The mutant removes only the analyzer-authored message, so the engine's `Syntax error (...)` survives and a fixture that merely counted errors would still pass; the fixture pins the analyzer's message verbatim, so this is caught. This is the mirror of the svelte lane's `namedChild` blindness: there the analyzer walked too few nodes, here it contributed nothing at all.

ERROR RECOVERY: the recovery region is turned into a SYMBOL. `ERROR` and `MISSING` are DIAGNOSTICS, not document constructs — they exist only where the parser could not read the source, and a node named after one joins to nothing a consumer can navigate to, which is the unresolvable-identity class reached through a malformed file rather than a missing edge. The companion half of the contract ("the region is REPORTED") is the engine's job — the toml analyzer pushes no errors of its own, so a mutation of analyzer output cannot remove a diagnostic; the fixture pins both and the mutant covers the half a mutant can reach. The fixture also pins what matters most and is easiest to get wrong: a walk that STOPPED at the recovery node would publish `t` and `t.before` and nothing after, and the document would still look analysed because its module is present. Caught by toml/malformed-and-rejected.

BARE-WRITABILITY, NOT PUNCTUATION: a path segment is quoted only when it contains `.`, `"` or `\`, so a segment that CANNOT be written bare is emitted bare. `[target."cfg(unix)".dependencies]` is real cargo syntax and `cfg(unix)` contains PARENTHESES — no punctuation the character test looks for — so the name came out `target.cfg(unix).dependencies`, which is not a spelling TOML can parse back. The same hole let a segment containing a SPACE through. Found by the differential oracle on cargo's own Cargo.toml, which is the argument for deriving the rule from the specification ("may this be written bare?") rather than from the characters that appear in the sample you happened to test. Caught by toml/dotted-and-quoted-paths.

ONE FUNCTION OWNS A PATH'S SPELLING: the ancestor lookup deciding which DECLARED table owns a section builds prefixes from RAW segments, while the declared-path table is keyed by the QUOTED spelling, so `target.cfg(unix).dependencies` never matches `target."cfg(unix)".dependencies` and a declared ancestor is reported as implied. The section is then filed under the MODULE. The symbol's NAME stays correct — the emit path does quote — so only the CONTAINMENT is wrong, which is why no symbol assertion could see it and why the fixture pins the edge's SOURCE. On cargo's Cargo.toml, `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies.windows-sys]` was filed under the module rather than the parent declared three lines earlier. Caught by toml/dotted-and-quoted-paths.

TOML-IDENTITY: a symbol's name becomes its LAST SEGMENT instead of its full dotted path, so `[workspace.lints.rust]` is `rust` and `package.name` is `name`. The first manifest anyone writes collides — cargo's own has a key named `name` under `[package]` AND under every `[[bin]]` — so the flattened names are not unique and a `contains` edge naming `name` resolves to two nodes. The full path is what makes a file's names unique without a synthetic suffix on every collision. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths.

TOML-IDENTITY: a quoted key segment is joined like a bare one, so a segment containing a dot loses its quotes. Inside `[t]`, `a.b.c` and `"a.b".c` are DIFFERENT TOML keys — three nested tables versus a table literally named `a.b` — and both assemble to `t.a.b.c`, after which the dedupe invents `t.a.b.c#2` and asserts the document declared one key twice when it declared two distinct ones. That is the unresolvable-identity class arriving through the NAMING SCHEME rather than through a missing edge, and re-quoting is TOML's own disambiguation, not an invented escape. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths, which writes all three spellings side by side.

IDENTITY: the module does not own its name in its own file, so a table may take the file's stem. `doc/book/book.toml` declares `[book]`, and relationships address nodes by NAME, so every `contains` edge naming `book` resolves to two nodes. The module's identity comes from its PATH and is not negotiable. This is html's precedence exactly (its `usedNames` starts `{ [moduleName]: 1 }`), and the rule was found by the CORPUS rather than by a fixture: 2 collisions in 684 cargo files, both `<stem>.toml` containing `[<stem>]`. Caught by toml/module-name-collision.

IMPLIED PARENTS: `[workspace.lints.rust]` invents symbols for `workspace` and `workspace.lints`, which the file never declares. The ruling is that they are RECORDED in `metadata.impliedParents` precisely because fabricating a table is a guess dressed as a fact — the graph would claim the document contains headers it does not, and a consumer diffing a config against its graph would see phantom entries. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths's forbidSymbols.

INLINE-TABLE SCOPING: an inline table's keys become symbols of the file. The ruling is that they are part of ONE value expression — `x = { a = 1 }` makes `x` the symbol — and a manifest with 200 dependencies written as `{ version = "...", features = [...] }` would publish 600+ symbols naming nothing a consumer can navigate to alone. Their names are recorded on the key in `metadata.inlineKeys`, so this mutant loses information as well as adding noise. Caught by toml/arrays-and-values.

ERROR RECOVERY: the walk STOPS at the first recovery node instead of bypassing it. `n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing` is the contract — report the region, skip it, keep publishing. Stopping instead means a document with one unreadable region publishes its module and the elements ABOVE the error and nothing below, and because the module still publishes the file still reads as analysed. A silent truncation is the defect class here, and it is invisible to every other gate in the lane because nothing counts symbols-per-file against a floor. Caught by html/error-recovery, whose fixture places the ERROR region in the MIDDLE of the document specifically so the half-after-the-error case is the one being tested.

CARRIER COMPLETENESS: the `<meta http-equiv=refresh>` navigation is dropped. The pragma makes the browser navigate — a form-action-class dependency, `uses` not `calls` — and it was absent from the table entirely: 40 occurrences across 26 files of one real corpus, found by a census of 4,035 files for URL-bearing (tag, attr) pairs. Invisible to the differential because the oracle SHARED the carrier list, and to `otp`/`sqlite` because neither corpus contains one. Caught by html/undiscovered-carriers.

CARRIER COMPLETENESS: `<a ping>` is read as ONE url instead of a whitespace-separated list, so `ping="/a /b"` publishes a single edge whose target is the whole string `"/a /b"` — a path that resolves to no file, which is the unresolvable-identity class reached through a list that was never split. The list shape IS the contract: `ping` has no descriptor and no comma, which is what separates it from `srcset`. Caught by html/undiscovered-carriers.

CARRIER COMPLETENESS: the SVG spellings go away — `script@href` and `feImage@href`/`xlink:href`. SVG2 writes a script's source as `href`, not `src`, so a table with `src` alone drops every inline SVG script's dependency and every filter image reference with it. Caught by html/undiscovered-carriers.

EVIDENCE TIER: a `cite` inherits `import_based` rather than `usage_contextual`. A citation names where a quotation or a change came FROM — nothing fetches it, nothing navigates to it — so grading it as a structural import overstates the fact, and the tier classifier in every gated lane reads this field, which makes the overstatement machine-readable. Caught by html/undiscovered-carriers.
